definition_zh: 极坏的；糟透的；深不见底的；极度糟糕的
definition_en: extremely bad or poor in quality, and in older use also meaning immeasurably deep
core_image: 一口望不到底的黑色竖井，井壁上连一丝光都抓不住
scene: 连续几场暴雨之后，球队在泥地里连丢五球，看台上的人陆续离场。The coach called the team's abysmal defending unacceptable at this level.
sceneCN: 这里 abysmal 指表现糟糕到几乎没有底线（第 1 个义项：极差的质量）；句意为教练称球队糟糕透顶的防守在这个水平上不可接受。

pos.zh: 极坏的；糟透的；深不可测的

senses.title: Extremely bad in quality
senses.definition: so bad in quality that it seems to have no bottom or limit
senses.definitionCN: 质量差到几乎看不到底线
senses.example: The food at that restaurant was abysmal.
senses.exampleCN: 那家餐厅的饭菜糟糕透顶。
senses.why: The word began as a description of physical depth; speakers later moved the image from a deep pit to a deep failure.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原本描述物理上的深度；说话者后来把「深坑」的形象移到了「深重的失败」上。

senses.title: Immeasurably deep
senses.definition: of a place or opening, so deep that its bottom cannot be reached or seen
senses.definitionCN: 指某个空间或开口深到无法触及或看见底部
senses.example: The explorers stared into an abysmal crack in the ice.
senses.exampleCN: 探险者凝视着冰面上那道深不见底的裂缝。
senses.why: This is the oldest physical sense: the adjective simply said that something had the quality of an abyss.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的物理义：形容词只是说某物具有「深渊」的性质。

senses.title: Utter ignorance
senses.definition: a complete and hopeless lack of knowledge or understanding
senses.definitionCN: 知识或理解上彻底而无可救药的匮乏
senses.example: His abysmal ignorance of basic geography embarrassed the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 他对基础地理的极度无知让整个团队难堪。
senses.why: Knowledge is treated as a container: when it is empty all the way down, the emptiness is described as bottomless.
senses.whyCN: 知识被当成一个容器：当它从上到下都是空的，这种空缺就被说成「无底」。

senses.title: Deplorable conditions
senses.definition: living or working conditions that are shockingly poor
senses.definitionCN: 居住或工作条件差得令人震惊
senses.example: The workers endured abysmal conditions in the old factory.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们在旧工厂里忍受着恶劣的条件。
senses.why: The image shifts from an empty mind to an empty place, and the place is judged by how far below a decent standard it falls.
senses.whyCN: 形象从「空空的头脑」转到「空空的场所」，而判断标准是它低于体面水平有多远。

senses.title: The lowest standard
senses.definition: a level of achievement or service that is far below what is expected
senses.definitionCN: 成绩或服务远低于应有水准
senses.example: The report described the hospital's record keeping as abysmal.
senses.exampleCN: 报告称这家医院的病历记录水平极低。
senses.why: A standard is a line drawn across a scale; when results fall far below that line, the fall is pictured as a plunge into depth.
senses.whyCN: 标准是刻度上的一条线；当结果远低于这条线时，这种下坠就被想象成跌入深处。

senses.title: A profound failure
senses.definition: a failure so complete that it seems to have no recoverable bottom
senses.definitionCN: 失败得如此彻底，仿佛没有可以重新站立的底部
senses.example: The launch was an abysmal failure and cost the firm its reputation.
senses.exampleCN: 这次发布是一次惨重失败，让公司失去了声誉。
senses.why: Failure is felt as a fall; the deeper the fall, the harder it is to climb back, so the word supplies the sense of no return.
senses.whyCN: 失败被感受为一次坠落；落得越深越难爬回，因此这个词带上了「无法回头」的意味。

senses.title: Miserable weather or setting
senses.definition: weather or surroundings that are bleak, wet and thoroughly unpleasant
senses.definitionCN: 天气或环境阴冷潮湿、令人极不愉快
senses.example: We spent the holiday in abysmal rain and never left the hotel.
senses.exampleCN: 我们整个假期都困在恶劣的阴雨里，始终没离开旅馆。
senses.why: The physical sense survives in descriptions of landscape: a grey sky and endless rain feel like a pit without a bottom.
senses.whyCN: 物理义在景物描写中保留下来：灰暗的天空和无休止的雨，感觉就像一口没有底的深坑。

senses.title: The abyss itself, in old use
senses.definition: in older writing, the bottomless void or the underworld imagined as a pit
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的文本中，指无底的虚空或被想象成深坑的冥界
senses.example: Milton's lines place chaos in an abysmal region below the world.
senses.exampleCN: 弥尔顿的诗句把混沌放在世界之下一个深渊般的区域。
senses.why: Before the adjective meant poor quality, it described the abyss of early cosmology, a place with no floor and no limit.
senses.whyCN: 在形容词表示「质量差」之前，它描述的是早期宇宙观中的深渊：一个没有底、没有边界的所在。

intro.en: Abysmal belongs to the old imagery of a bottomless pit. It first described physical depth and only later became a word for very poor quality.
intro.cn: abysmal 属于「无底深坑」这一古老意象。它最初描述物理深度，后来才变成表示质量极差的词。

items.en: From the 19c. the adjective is applied figuratively to failures and conditions, and by the 20c. 'very bad' is the dominant sense in speech.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个形容词被比喻性地用于失败与境况；到二十世纪，「极差」已成为口语中的主导义。

items.en: Late Latin abysmalis and abyssimus were formed from abyssus, the Latin church word for the bottomless deep of Genesis.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 abysmalis 与 abyssimus 由 abyssus 构成，后者是拉丁教会在《创世记》中用来指无底深渊的词。

items.en: Greek abyssos meant 'bottomless, unfathomable', used of the sea and of the deep in early Christian writing.
items.cn: 希腊语 abyssos 意为「无底的、不可测的」，早期基督教文献用它指大海与深渊。

items.en: The Greek word is a- 'not, without' plus byssos 'depth, bottom'. The same byssos later gave English byssal, a term for a fine thread.
items.cn: 这个希腊词由 a-「无、没有」加 byssos「深度、底部」构成。同一个 byssos 后来还产生了英语 byssal，指细丝。

items.en: English took the word through Latin translations of the Bible, so abyss and abysmal entered the language with a theological charge before they became everyday intensifiers.
items.cn: 英语经由《圣经》的拉丁译本吸收此词，因此 abyss 与 abysmal 进入英语时带着神学色彩，之后才成为日常的强调词。

note.en: The first group shares letters or a root with abysmal; the second group shares the idea of being very bad.
note.cn: 第一组与 abysmal 共享字母或词根；第二组共享「非常糟糕」这一含义。

entries.definition: the bottomless deep; a very deep hole. It is the noun behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 无底的深渊；极深的洞。它是这个形容词背后的名词。

entries.definition: relating to the deepest ocean zone, not to bad quality.
entries.definitionCN: 与最深的海域有关，与质量差无关。

entries.definition: in an extremely bad way. It adds the adverb ending to the same adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 以极差的方式。它在同一个形容词后加副词词尾。

entries.definition: an older spelling of abyss, now rare in ordinary text.
entries.definitionCN: abyss 的旧拼写，现代普通文本已罕见。

entries.definition: shockingly bad or cruel; often used of behaviour or quality.
entries.definitionCN: 骇人地糟糕或残忍；常用于行为或质量。

entries.definition: extremely bad or unpleasant, in a milder everyday tone.
entries.definitionCN: 极坏或极不愉快，语气在日常中稍轻。

entries.definition: so bad that it causes shock and disgust.
entries.definitionCN: 差到令人震惊和厌恶。

entries.definition: bleak, gloomy and poor in quality, often of conditions or results.
entries.definitionCN: 阴郁、黯淡且质量差，常指境况或结果。

normalIntro.en: These hooks link the spelling to the image of a pit with no floor.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些联想把拼写和「没有底的深坑」这一形象连起来。

normal.en: abyss plus al: an abyss is a bottomless pit, so abysmal means as bad as a pit with no floor.
normal.cn: abyss 加 al：abyss 是无底深坑，所以 abysmal 就是「差得像没有底的坑」。

normal.en: Think of the letters a-b-y-s-s: a, by, ss, a fall that never stops.
normal.cn: 记字母 a-b-y-s-s：a、by、ss，像一次停不下来的下坠。

normal.en: A bad score is a fall; an abysmal score is a fall with no bottom.
normal.cn: 差分数是一次下坠；abysmal 的分数是看不到底的下坠。

normal.en: Say abysmal slowly: the stress falls on the second syllable, like a stone dropping.
normal.cn: 慢慢读 abysmal：重音落在第二个音节，像石头往下掉。

normal.en: Link it with the noun abyss you already know from geography texts.
normal.cn: 把它和地理课本里学过的名词 abyss 联系起来。

abstract.en: Depth becomes value: the deeper the failure, the lower the quality.
abstract.cn: 深度变成价值：失败越深，质量越低。

abstract.en: A container image: an empty mind all the way down is bottomless ignorance.
abstract.cn: 容器意象：从上到下都空的头脑，就是无底的无知。

abstract.en: No floor means no recovery, which is why the word feels stronger than merely bad.
abstract.cn: 没有底就意味着无法恢复，所以这个词比单纯的 bad 更有力。

examples.en: The team's abysmal defending cost them the match.
examples.cn: 球队糟糕透顶的防守让他们输掉了比赛。

examples.en: Living conditions in the camp were abysmal.
examples.cn: 营地里的生活条件极其恶劣。

examples.en: He showed an abysmal lack of preparation for the interview.
examples.cn: 他在面试中表现出极度的准备不足。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 abyss（深渊）加 -al 记成「深到没底」，再引申为「差到没底」。

root: 希腊语 abyssos（无底深渊）：a-（无）+ byssos（深度）

sensesIntro.en: Abysmal has one physical core, depth without a bottom, and several figurative extensions in which that depth measures failure, ignorance or poor conditions.
sensesIntro.cn: abysmal 只有一个物理核心，即「没有底的深度」，其余义项都是引申：用这种深度来衡量失败、无知或恶劣条件。

branches.en: Depth itself, first physical and then figurative.
branches.cn: 先是物理深度，随后转为比喻性的深。

branches.en: Emptiness all the way down becomes extreme ignorance.
branches.cn: 从上到下的空缺变成极度的无知。

branches.en: A place or setting judged to be far below a decent level.
branches.cn: 场所或环境被判定远低于体面水平。

branches.en: A standard missed so badly that the result is a deep failure.
branches.cn: 严重未达标准，结果成为深重的失败。

branches.en: The old cosmological abyss, kept in literary description.
branches.cn: 古老的宇宙论深渊，保留在文学描写中。

intro.en: The word is built from a Greek negative prefix, a Greek root for depth, and an English adjective ending.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个希腊否定前缀、一个表示深度的希腊词根和一个英语形容词词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin and Greek entries show how the idea travelled from sea depth to church language and then to English.
latinIntro.cn: 下面这些拉丁语与希腊语条目展示这一概念如何从海洋深度进入教会语言，再进入英语。

items.meaning: without a bottom, hence extremely deep or bad
items.meaningCN: 没有底，因而极深或极坏

items.example: The ship sank into the abyss.

items.meaning: relating to the abyss or the deep sea
items.example: Abyssal creatures live far below the surface.
items.exampleCN: 深海生物生活在海面以下很远的地方。

items.example: The old poem speaks of an abysm of fire.
items.exampleCN: 那首古老的诗提到火焰的深渊。

items.meaning: relating to, having the quality of

latinEntries.meaning: bottomless deep, the deep of scripture
latinEntries.meaningCN: 无底的深处，经文中的深渊

definition_zh: 审理；裁决；裁定；担任裁判
definition_en: to hear and decide a case or dispute officially, or to act as the judge of a competition
core_image: 一张摆着卷宗的桌子，桌后的人敲下木槌，把两边争持的线画成一条
scene: 两家公司为一块地的边界争了三年，最后把材料交到仲裁庭。The tribunal will adjudicate the boundary dispute next month.
sceneCN: 这里 adjudicate 指由第三方正式审理并作出裁决（第 1 个义项：审理案件）；句意为仲裁庭将在下个月裁决这起边界争议。

senses.title: Hear and decide a case
senses.definition: to examine a legal case and give an official decision on it
senses.definitionCN: 审查法律案件并作出正式决定
senses.example: The court agreed to adjudicate the bankruptcy case.
senses.exampleCN: 法院同意审理这起破产案件。
senses.why: The Latin verb joined 'to' with 'to judge': the judge is brought to the matter so that a decision can be fixed.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词把「向」和「审判」连在一起：把审判者带到事情面前，好让决定被固定下来。

senses.title: Settle a dispute
senses.definition: to settle a disagreement between parties by an authoritative decision
senses.definitionCN: 以权威决定解决各方之间的分歧
senses.example: An independent panel was appointed to adjudicate the dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 一个独立小组被指定来裁决这场争议。
senses.why: A dispute is two claims pulling in opposite directions; adjudication cuts the line between them.
senses.whyCN: 争议是两个主张朝相反方向拉扯；裁决在它们之间划下界线。

senses.title: Rule on a claim or right
senses.definition: to decide whether a claim, right or objection is valid
senses.definitionCN: 判定某项主张、权利或异议是否成立
senses.example: The agency adjudicated her claim for compensation.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构裁定她的赔偿主张。
senses.why: A claim is a demand held up for recognition; the judge either confirms it or lets it fall.
senses.whyCN: 主张是一个举起来等待承认的要求；审判者要么确认它，要么让它落下。

senses.title: Act as a judge
senses.definition: to serve in the role of judge at a hearing or formal proceeding
senses.definitionCN: 在听证或正式程序中担任审判者角色
senses.example: A retired justice will adjudicate at the final hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 一位退休法官将在最终听证会上担任裁判。
senses.why: Here the verb names the office rather than the single act: the person is placed in the judging seat.
senses.whyCN: 这里动词命名的是职位而不是单次动作：这个人被安置在审判席上。

senses.title: Judge a competition
senses.definition: to assess entries or performances in a contest and decide the winners
senses.definitionCN: 评比比赛中的作品或表演并决定优胜者
senses.example: Three composers were invited to adjudicate the piano contest.
senses.exampleCN: 三位作曲家受邀来评定这场钢琴比赛。
senses.why: The contest is a field of rival claims; the adjudicator turns many claims into one ranking.
senses.whyCN: 比赛是一片相互竞争的主张；裁判把许多主张变成一个名次。

senses.title: Award a prize officially
senses.definition: to officially decide that a prize or title belongs to a particular person
senses.definitionCN: 正式判定某项奖赏或头衔归某人所有
senses.example: The committee adjudicated the scholarship to the youngest applicant.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会把奖学金判给了最年轻的申请人。
senses.why: The decision transfers a thing from the group to one holder, which is the judging act at its most concrete.
senses.whyCN: 这个决定把一件东西从集体转到某个持有者手里，这是审判行为最具体的形态。

senses.title: Rule in a bankruptcy or tribunal
senses.definition: to determine the legal status of a debtor, claim or proceeding in a tribunal
senses.definitionCN: 在审裁机构中确定债务人、债权或程序的法律地位
senses.example: The tribunal adjudicated the company insolvent.
senses.exampleCN: 审裁庭裁定该公司破产。
senses.why: A status is not a thing one can see; it exists only after an authority declares it, so the verb creates the status it names.
senses.whyCN: 地位不是肉眼可见之物；它只在权威宣布之后才存在，因此这个动词创造了它所命名的地位。

senses.title: Give an official ruling
senses.definition: to issue a formal ruling that binds the parties, whether or not they accept it
senses.definitionCN: 发布对各方有约束力的正式裁定，无论他们是否接受
senses.example: The board adjudicated that the contract was void.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会裁定该合同无效。
senses.why: The last step is the binding word: once spoken by the right body, the decision stops being an opinion and becomes an order.
senses.whyCN: 最后一步是有约束力的话语：一旦由正确的机构说出，决定就不再是意见，而成为命令。

intro.en: Adjudicate is a Latin legal verb built from 'to' and 'to judge'. Its family includes judge, judicial and prejudice.
intro.cn: adjudicate 是一个由「向」和「审判」构成的拉丁法律动词。它的同族词包括 judge、judicial 与 prejudice。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the 17c. from Latin adjudicare, first in legal writing and later in competition language.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪从拉丁语 adjudicare 借入这个动词，先用于法律文本，后来进入比赛用语。

items.en: Adjudicare meant 'to give by judgement, award, decide'. The prefix ad- 'to' shows the judge directing the decision toward a person or thing.
items.cn: adjudicare 意为「凭审判给予、判给、裁定」。前缀 ad-「向」表示审判者把决定指向某人或某物。

items.en: Judicare 'to judge' comes from judex, a compound of jus 'law, right' and dicere 'to say, declare'.
items.cn: judicare「审判」来自 judex，由 jus「法、权利」与 dicere「说、宣告」复合而成。

items.en: The phrase jus dicere, literally 'to say the law', is the origin of the judge's role: the law is spoken into a particular case.
items.cn: 短语 jus dicere 字面意为「说出法律」，这正是审判者角色的来源：法律被说进具体案件之中。

items.en: The noun adjudication and the agent adjudicator keep the courtroom image, while sport and music contests extend it to any ranked decision.
items.cn: 名词 adjudication 与施动者 adjudicator 保留法庭意象，而体育与音乐比赛把它扩展到任何排名决定。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin judging root; the near-meaning group names people or acts that decide disputes.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁「审判」词根；近义组列出决定争议的人或行为。

entries.definition: the official decision reached after hearing a case.
entries.definitionCN: 审理案件后作出的正式决定。

entries.definition: the person who hears and decides a case or contest.
entries.definitionCN: 审理并裁决案件或比赛的人。

entries.definition: relating to the work of deciding cases.
entries.definitionCN: 与裁决案件的工作有关。

entries.definition: relating to courts and judges, from the same Latin judex.
entries.definitionCN: 与法院和法官有关，来自同一个拉丁词 judex。

entries.definition: to settle a dispute as a neutral third party.
entries.definitionCN: 作为中立第三方解决争议。

entries.definition: to form and pronounce a decision about a case or person.
entries.definitionCN: 对案件或人形成并宣布决定。

entries.definition: to make an official decision on a point of law or procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 对法律或程序问题作出正式决定。

entries.definition: to bring a disagreement to an end by agreement or decision.
entries.definitionCN: 通过协议或决定结束分歧。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the judge's hammer and the 'to' prefix in view.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把法官的木槌和前缀「向」留在眼前。

normal.en: ad plus judge: the judge is brought ad, that is 'to', the case.
normal.cn: ad 加 judge：审判者被带到案件那里，ad 就是「向」。

normal.en: Picture a gavel hitting the desk; that sound is the moment a dispute becomes a ruling.
normal.cn: 想象木槌敲在桌上；那一声就是争议变成裁定的瞬间。

normal.en: The ending -ate marks a verb, so adjudicate is the act, adjudication is the result.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ate 标记动词，所以 adjudicate 是动作，adjudication 是结果。

normal.en: Say the four syllables as a court sequence: ad, ju, di, cate.
normal.cn: 把四个音节读成法庭流程：ad、ju、di、cate。

normal.en: Link it with judge and judicial, both from the same Latin word for law-speaking.
normal.cn: 把它和 judge、judicial 联系起来，二者都来自同一个表示「说出法律」的拉丁词。

abstract.en: A dispute is two arrows; adjudication draws the line they cannot cross.
abstract.cn: 争议是两支箭头；裁决画出它们不能越过的界线。

abstract.en: A status such as insolvent exists only after it is declared, so the verb makes what it names.
abstract.cn: 像「破产」这样的地位只在被宣布后才存在，因此这个动词创造了它所命名之物。

abstract.en: Authority is the difference between an opinion and a ruling.
abstract.cn: 权威就是意见与裁定之间的差别。

examples.en: The court will adjudicate the dispute between the two firms.
examples.cn: 法院将裁决两家公司之间的争议。

examples.en: She was chosen to adjudicate the national debating final.
examples.cn: 她被选中担任全国辩论决赛的裁判。

examples.en: The tribunal adjudicated that the debt had been discharged.
examples.cn: 审裁庭裁定该债务已经解除。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses keep one action, an authority cutting a decision into a disputed matter; the differences lie in what is being decided.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留同一个动作：权威把决定切进有争议的事情里；差别只在决定的对象。

branches.en: The hearing and the binding ruling that ends it.
branches.cn: 审理过程以及结束它的约束性裁定。

branches.en: Disputes and claims are the two things most often cut apart.
branches.cn: 争议与主张是最常被切开的两种对象。

branches.en: The judge as an office, and the contest as a field of rankings.
branches.cn: 作为职位的审判者，以及作为排名场域的比赛。

branches.en: Awarding a thing to one holder, and declaring a legal status.
branches.cn: 把某物判给一个持有者，以及宣布某种法律地位。

branches.cn: 把意见变成命令的那句宣告。

definition_zh: 利他主义；无私；为他人着想的行为
definition_en: the belief or practice of caring for others' welfare more than one's own, often at personal cost
core_image: 一个人把手里最后一块面包递出去，自己的影子却留在空盘子上
scene: 洪水退去后，志愿者把自己的帐篷让给带孩子的家庭，自己在屋檐下坐了一夜。Her quiet altruism surprised no one who knew her.
sceneCN: 这里 altruism 指把他人的福祉放在自己之前的无私行为（第 1 个义项：无私关怀）；句意为她安静无声的利他之举，认识她的人都不意外。

pos.zh: 利他主义；无私；利他行为

senses.title: Selfless concern for others
senses.definition: the attitude of caring about other people's welfare without expecting a reward
senses.definitionCN: 关心他人福祉而不期待回报的态度
senses.example: Her altruism was rooted in a childhood of shared scarcity.
senses.exampleCN: 她的无私源于童年时共同经历的匮乏。
senses.why: The word was coined as a moral counterweight to egoism: one pole names the self, the other names the other person.
senses.whyCN: 这个词被造出来，是为了与利己主义相抗衡：一极命名自我，另一极命名他人。

senses.title: Helping at personal cost
senses.definition: an act that benefits another person while costing the helper time, money or safety
senses.definitionCN: 使他人受益、却让帮助者付出时间、金钱或安全的行为
senses.example: He performed an act of altruism by paying her tuition anonymously.
senses.exampleCN: 他匿名替她付学费，做了一件利他之举。
senses.why: The core is not a feeling but a transfer: something passes from the helper to the helped, and the helper keeps the loss.
senses.whyCN: 核心不是感受，而是转移：某物从帮助者转到受助者，而帮助者留下损失。

senses.title: Biological altruism
senses.definition: in biology, behaviour that lowers an individual's own fitness while raising another's
senses.definitionCN: 在生物学中，指降低个体自身适应度却提高他者适应度的行为
senses.example: Biologists study altruism in ants that die defending the colony.
senses.exampleCN: 生物学家研究蚂蚁为保卫群体而死这种利他行为。
senses.why: A gene's survival can be served by helping relatives, so the cost to one body may still be a gain to the shared line.
senses.whyCN: 基因的延续可以通过帮助亲属实现，因此一个个体的代价仍可能是共同血脉的收益。

senses.title: A moral principle
senses.definition: a principle that tells people to weigh others' interests equally with their own
senses.definitionCN: 要求人们把他人的利益与自身利益同等权衡的原则
senses.example: The lecture contrasted altruism with utilitarianism.
senses.exampleCN: 讲座把利他主义与功利主义对照讲解。
senses.why: Once an attitude becomes a rule, it can be taught and argued about, which is why it appears in ethics textbooks.
senses.whyCN: 当一种态度变成规则，它就可以被教授和争论，因此出现在伦理学教科书里。

senses.title: Charitable giving
senses.definition: donating money, goods or time to strangers without direct benefit
senses.definitionCN: 向陌生人捐赠金钱、物品或时间而无直接收益
senses.example: The foundation was built on the altruism of a few donors.
senses.exampleCN: 这个基金会建立在少数捐赠者的无私之上。
senses.why: Modern charity makes the transfer large and anonymous, so the old word is stretched to cover gifts to people one will never meet.
senses.whyCN: 现代慈善让转移变得巨大而匿名，于是这个旧词被扩展到「给永远不会见面的人送礼」。

senses.title: Everyday kindness
senses.definition: small helpful acts in ordinary life that ask for no return
senses.definitionCN: 日常生活中不求回报的小小帮助
senses.example: Offering a seat on a crowded train is a small act of altruism.
senses.exampleCN: 在拥挤的火车上让座，是一件小小的利他之举。
senses.why: The scale shrinks but the shape stays: a cost is taken on so that another person's moment improves.
senses.whyCN: 规模缩小了，但形状不变：接受一份代价，让另一个人的时刻变好。

senses.title: Organizational altruism
senses.definition: a company or institution giving up some advantage for the good of a wider group
senses.definitionCN: 公司或机构为更大群体的利益放弃部分优势
senses.example: The firm's decision to share its patent was praised as corporate altruism.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司决定共享专利，被称赞为企业利他。
senses.why: An institution repeats the personal pattern at a larger scale: it gives up an advantage so that a wider group benefits.
senses.whyCN: 机构在更大尺度上重复个人的模式：放弃一项优势，让更广泛的群体受益。

senses.title: A philosophical idea
senses.definition: the philosophical claim that disinterested action for others is possible and morally valuable
senses.definitionCN: 认为为他人的无私行为既可能又有道德价值的哲学主张
senses.example: The debate asked whether altruism can ever be entirely disinterested.
senses.exampleCN: 这场辩论追问利他是否可能完全不带私心。
senses.why: The final step is abstract: once the transfer is studied as a claim about human nature, it becomes a question for philosophy.
senses.whyCN: 最后一步是抽象化：当这种转移被当作关于人性的主张来研究，它就成了哲学问题。

intro.en: Altruism is a modern coined word, not an inherited one. It was built in French from a Latin word for 'other'.
intro.cn: altruism 是一个现代新造词，而不是继承来的词。它在法语中用拉丁语「他人」一词构造而成。

items.en: English adopted altruism in the mid 19c. as the direct opposite of egoism in moral and social writing.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪中期吸收 altruism，在道德与社会文本中作为 egoism 的直接对立词。

items.en: The French philosopher Auguste Comte coined altruisme around 1830 from autrui 'other people'.
items.cn: 法国哲学家奥古斯特·孔德约在 1830 年用 autrui「他人」造出 altruisme。

items.en: Autrui comes from the Old French phrase altrui, a case form of autre 'other'.
items.cn: autrui 来自古法语短语 altrui，是 autre「其他」的格变形式。

items.en: The Latin source is alter 'the other of two', which also gives English alternative and alternate.
items.cn: 其拉丁语来源是 alter「两者中的另一个」，它也产生了英语 alternative 与 alternate。

items.en: Comte's coinage was meant to name a secular virtue, so the word entered English already carrying a philosophical programme.
items.cn: 孔德的造词意在命名一种世俗美德，因此这个词进入英语时已带着一套哲学纲领。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin root for 'other'; the second group names related moral qualities.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「他人」词根；第二组列出相关的道德品质。

entries.definition: a person who acts with altruism.
entries.definitionCN: 以利他方式行事的人。

entries.definition: showing altruism; selfless.
entries.definitionCN: 表现出利他的；无私的。

entries.definition: in a selfless way.
entries.definitionCN: 以无私的方式。

entries.definition: to change, from Latin alter 'other'; the root also underlies alternative.
entries.definitionCN: 改变，来自拉丁语 alter「其他」；这个词根也构成 alternative。

entries.definition: the quality of putting others before oneself.
entries.definitionCN: 把他人放在自己之前的品质。

entries.definition: kindness and goodwill toward others.
entries.definitionCN: 对他人的善意与好心。

entries.definition: giving help or money to those in need.
entries.definitionCN: 向有需要者提供帮助或金钱。

entries.definition: willingness to give freely, often of money or time.
entries.definitionCN: 乐于慷慨给予，常指金钱或时间。

normalIntro.en: The hooks tie the word to 'other people' and to the picture of handing something over.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把这个词和「他人」以及「把东西递出去」的画面绑在一起。

normal.en: Altruism contains alter, Latin for 'other': the focus is on the other person.
normal.cn: altruism 里有 alter，拉丁语意为「其他」：焦点在他人身上。

normal.en: Picture the last piece of bread leaving your hand; that transfer is the word.
normal.cn: 想象最后一块面包离开你的手；那次转移就是这个单词。

normal.en: The ending -ism marks a principle, so altruism is both an act and a belief.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ism 标记一种原则，所以 altruism 既是行为也是信念。

normal.en: Pair it with egoism: ego is self, alter is other.
normal.cn: 把它和 egoism 配对记：ego 是自我，alter 是他人。

normal.en: Say the first syllable as 'alt', as if you are handing over an alternative life.
normal.cn: 把第一个音节读成 alt，好像你在交出另一种人生。

abstract.en: A transfer with a cost: the helper loses something so the helped gains.
abstract.cn: 带代价的转移：帮助者失去一些，受助者得到一些。

abstract.en: Biology reframes the cost as a gain for shared genes.
abstract.cn: 生物学把这个代价重新解释为共享基因的收益。

abstract.en: When the transfer is anonymous and large, it becomes charity.
abstract.cn: 当转移匿名且规模巨大时，它就成了慈善。

examples.en: Her altruism led her to fund the clinic anonymously.
examples.cn: 她的无私使她匿名资助了这家诊所。

examples.en: Reciprocal altruism can explain cooperation among unrelated animals.
examples.cn: 互惠利他可以解释无亲缘关系动物之间的合作。

examples.en: The essay asks whether pure altruism is possible.
examples.cn: 这篇文章追问纯粹的利他是否可能。

dict_mnemonic.text: alter（他人）+ ism（主义）：把他人放在自己之前的主义，就是利他主义。

root: 法语 altruisme，由 autrui（他人）构成，源自拉丁语 alter（两者中的另一个）

sensesIntro.en: Altruism always describes a transfer that costs the giver; the senses differ in scale, from a seat on a train to a principle of ethics.
sensesIntro.cn: altruism 始终描述一种让给予者付出代价的转移；各义项的差别在规模，从火车上的一个座位到一条伦理原则。

branches.en: The everyday attitude and its small acts.
branches.cn: 日常态度及其小小行为。

branches.en: Costly help, from one gift to large anonymous charity.
branches.cn: 有代价的帮助，从一次赠予到大规模匿名慈善。

branches.en: Biology measures the cost in fitness and the gain in relatives.
branches.cn: 生物学用适应度衡量代价，用亲属衡量收益。

branches.en: The attitude turned into a rule and then into a debated idea.
branches.cn: 态度变成规则，再变成被争论的观念。

branches.cn: 机构在公司尺度上呈现同样的形状。

intro.cn: 这个词是法语在拉丁词根上的新造词，带一个英语名词词尾。

items.meaning: the principle of putting others first
items.meaningCN: 把他人放在首位的原则
items.example: Altruism can be taught by example.
items.exampleCN: 利他可以通过榜样来教。

items.exampleCN: 捐赠者坚称自己不是利他者。
她的利他之举没有被记录。
他在压力下仍以无私的方式行事。

items.meaningCN: 另一个、两者中的第二个
items.example: An alter ego is a second self.
items.exampleCN: alter ego 指第二个自我。
我们需要一个替代方案。

items.example: Egoism is the mirror of altruism.
items.exampleCN: 利己主义是利他主义的镜像。

definition_zh: 矛盾情绪；矛盾心态；既爱又恨；犹豫不决
definition_en: the state of having two opposite feelings or attitudes about the same person, thing or choice
core_image: 一个人同时向同一扇门伸出手和收回手，两只手都停在半空
scene: 她在旧屋门口站了很久，一只手想推门进去，另一只手却把钥匙握得更紧。Her ambivalence about selling the family house lasted for years.
sceneCN: 这里 ambivalence 指对同一件事同时怀有两种相反情绪（第 1 个义项：矛盾情绪）；句意为她对是否卖掉祖屋的矛盾心态持续了好几年。

pos.zh: 矛盾情绪；矛盾心态；犹豫不决

senses.title: Two opposite feelings at once
senses.titleCN: 同时怀有两种相反情绪
senses.definition: the coexistence of opposite feelings, such as love and resentment, toward one object
senses.definitionCN: 对同一对象同时存在相反情感，例如爱与怨恨
senses.example: She felt ambivalence toward the town that raised her.
senses.exampleCN: 她对养育自己的小镇怀着矛盾情绪。
senses.why: The word names two forces pulling at once: ambi- is 'both', and valentia is 'strength'.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名两股同时拉扯的力量：ambi- 是「两者」，valentia 是「力量」。

senses.title: Indecision between options
senses.definition: a state of being unable to choose because both options attract and repel
senses.definitionCN: 因为两个选项都既吸引又排斥而无法选择
senses.example: His ambivalence about the job offer delayed the reply for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 他对这份工作邀请的矛盾心态让回复拖了一周。
senses.why: Choice requires a preference; when two preferences hold equal weight, the scale does not tip.
senses.whyCN: 选择需要偏好；当两种偏好等重时，天平不会倾斜。

senses.title: Attraction and repulsion together
senses.definition: an emotional pull toward something that also causes discomfort or fear
senses.definitionCN: 对某物既被吸引又感到不适或恐惧
senses.example: There is a strange ambivalence in watching a storm from a safe room.
senses.exampleCN: 在安全的房间里看暴风雨，有一种奇怪的既吸引又排斥的感觉。
senses.why: Attraction and fear can hold the same object, which is the two-force structure at its most physical.
senses.whyCN: 吸引力与恐惧可以同时占据同一个对象，这是「两股力量」结构最具体的样子。

senses.title: Conflicting attitudes
senses.definition: the holding of two incompatible opinions or values about the same issue
senses.definitionCN: 对同一问题持有两种不相容的意见或价值
senses.example: Public ambivalence about the new tax shaped the debate.
senses.exampleCN: 公众对新税的冲突态度影响了这场辩论。
senses.why: Two opinions on one issue behave like two weights; when both are heavy, the attitude cannot settle.
senses.whyCN: 对同一问题的两种意见像两个砝码；两者都重时，态度无法稳定。

senses.title: A psychiatric term
senses.definition: in psychiatry, the simultaneous existence of contradictory impulses or feelings
senses.definitionCN: 在精神医学中，指相互矛盾的冲动或情感同时存在
senses.example: The clinician noted ambivalence as a feature of the patient's mood.
senses.exampleCN: 临床医生把矛盾情感记为病人情绪的一个特征。
senses.why: Clinical language names the same two-force conflict, but here it is observed as a symptom rather than a choice.
senses.whyCN: 临床语言命名的是同一种「两股力量」冲突，只是这里它被观察为症状，而不是选择。

senses.title: A public mood
senses.definition: a widespread mixture of approval and unease in a society
senses.definitionCN: 社会中普遍存在的赞同与不安的混合
senses.example: Surveys recorded ambivalence rather than clear support.
senses.exampleCN: 调查记录到的是矛盾心态，而不是明确支持。
senses.why: When many people hold the same mixed feeling, the private structure becomes a public climate.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人持有同一种混合感受时，私人的结构就变成公共的气候。

senses.title: A literary tone
senses.definition: a tone in writing that expresses affection and criticism at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 写作中同时表达亲近与批评的基调
senses.example: The novel's ambivalence toward its hero gives it depth.
senses.exampleCN: 小说对主人公的矛盾态度让它有了深度。
senses.why: A narrator can hold two attitudes without resolving them, and readers feel that suspension as tone.
senses.whyCN: 叙述者可以同时持有两种态度而不作解决，读者把这种悬置感受为基调。

senses.title: Uncertainty of choice
senses.definition: a lingering doubt that prevents a firm commitment
senses.definitionCN: 迟迟不去的疑虑使人无法坚定承诺
senses.example: Her ambivalence kept the engagement in limbo.
senses.exampleCN: 她的犹豫不决让婚约悬而未决。
senses.why: The two forces never settle, so the commitment stays suspended, which is the practical result of the structure.
senses.whyCN: 两股力量始终不落定，因此承诺一直悬着，这就是该结构在实际生活中的结果。

intro.en: Ambivalence is a modern psychiatric coinage built from two Latin pieces meaning 'both' and 'strength'.
intro.cn: ambivalence 是一个现代精神医学新造词，由两个拉丁语零件构成，分别表示「两者」与「力量」。

items.en: English borrowed the term in the early 20c. and soon widened it from clinical writing to ordinary emotional life.
items.cn: 英语在二十世纪初借入该术语，很快把它从临床文本扩展到日常情感生活。

items.en: The Swiss psychiatrist Eugen Bleuler coined Ambivalenz in 1910 to describe contradictory impulses in schizophrenia.
items.cn: 瑞士精神科医生尤金·布洛伊勒于 1910 年造出 Ambivalenz，用来描述精神分裂症中的矛盾冲动。

items.en: The prefix ambi- means 'both, on both sides', as in ambidextrous and ambiguous.
items.cn: 前缀 ambi- 意为「两者、两边」，如 ambidextrous 与 ambiguous。

items.en: Valentia 'strength, power' comes from valere 'to be strong, be worth', which also gives value and valid.
items.cn: valentia「力量、能力」来自 valere「强壮、有价值」，它也产生了 value 与 valid。

items.en: From psychiatry the word spread to politics, criticism and everyday speech, where it usually means mixed feelings rather than illness.
items.cn: 从精神医学出发，这个词扩散到政治、批评与日常语言，通常表示混合情绪，而不是疾病。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the 'both' prefix or the same root; the near-meaning group names forms of doubt and conflict.
note.cn: 形近组共享「两者」前缀或同一词根；近义组列出怀疑与冲突的各种形态。

entries.definition: having mixed or opposite feelings.
entries.definitionCN: 怀有混合或相反情感的。

entries.definition: in a way that shows mixed feelings.
entries.definitionCN: 以表现矛盾情感的方式。

entries.definition: having more than one possible meaning; unclear.
entries.definitionCN: 有不止一种可能含义；不清楚。

entries.definition: able to use both hands equally well.
entries.definitionCN: 双手同样灵巧的。

entries.definition: the inability to make a decision.
entries.definitionCN: 无法作出决定。

entries.definition: a struggle between opposing forces or wishes.
entries.definitionCN: 对立力量或愿望之间的挣扎。

entries.definition: a state of not being sure what to think or do.
entries.definitionCN: 不确定该想什么或做什么的状态。

entries.definition: a feeling of not being convinced.
entries.definitionCN: 未被说服的感觉。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the 'both' prefix and the picture of two hands pulling one door.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想利用「两者」前缀和「两只手拉同一扇门」的画面。

normal.en: ambi means both, valence means strength: two strengths pulling at once.
normal.cn: ambi 意为两者，valence 意为力量：两股力量同时拉扯。

normal.en: Picture two hands on one door handle, one pushing in and one pulling back.
normal.cn: 想象两只手握在同一门把上，一只往里推，一只往回拉。

normal.en: The ending -ence makes it a state, so it is the condition of being pulled two ways.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ence 使它成为状态，即被两边拉扯的处境。

normal.en: Link it with ambiguous: both words begin with 'both'.
normal.cn: 把它和 ambiguous 联系起来：两个词都以「两者」开头。

normal.en: Say it as am-bi-valence, a balance that will not settle.
normal.cn: 读成 am-bi-valence，一架不肯停稳的天平。

abstract.en: A scale with equal weights cannot tip, and that stillness is the word.
abstract.cn: 两边的重量相等的天平不会倾斜，这种静止就是这个单词。

abstract.en: Love and resentment can occupy the same object without cancelling out.
abstract.cn: 爱与怨恨可以占据同一对象而不互相抵消。

abstract.en: Clinical use narrows the word; everyday use widens it back to mixed feelings.
abstract.cn: 临床用法使词义变窄；日常用法又把它扩回混合情绪。

examples.en: She described her ambivalence about leaving the city.
examples.cn: 她描述了自己对离开这座城市的矛盾心情。

examples.en: The novel treats modernity with ambivalence.
examples.cn: 这部小说以矛盾的笔调对待现代性。

examples.en: His ambivalence made the final decision harder.
examples.cn: 他的犹豫不决让最终决定更难作出。

dict_mnemonic.text: ambi（两者）+ valence（力量）：两股力量同时拉，就是「矛盾情绪」。

root: 德语 Ambivalenz，由拉丁语 ambi-（两者）+ valentia（力量）构成

sensesIntro.en: Ambivalence is one structure, two forces on the same object; the senses vary by whether the forces are feelings, opinions, choices or a clinical symptom.
sensesIntro.cn: ambivalence 只有一个结构，即两股力量作用在同一对象上；各义项的差别在于这两股力量是情感、意见、选择还是临床症状。

branches.en: The basic emotional mixture of attraction and resistance.
branches.cn: 吸引与抗拒的基本情绪混合。

branches.en: The choice that cannot be made and the doubt that remains.
branches.cn: 无法作出的选择以及留下的疑虑。

branches.en: Attitudes and public moods made of two incompatible halves.
branches.cn: 由两个不相容部分构成的态度与公众情绪。

branches.en: The clinical reading, where the conflict is a symptom.
branches.cn: 临床解读，其中冲突是一种症状。

branches.en: The literary tone that holds affection and criticism together.
branches.cn: 同时容纳亲近与批评的文学基调。

intro.en: The word is a German coinage on Latin pieces, so its parts are unusually transparent.
intro.cn: 这个词是德语在拉丁语零件上的新造词，因此各部分异常透明。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show the 'both' and 'strength' ideas inside the term.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁语条目展示术语内「两者」与「力量」两个概念。

items.example: Her ambivalence was plain to see.
items.exampleCN: 她的矛盾心态显而易见。

items.example: He was ambivalent about the move.
She spoke ambivalently of her success.
items.exampleCN: 她谈及自己的成功时语气矛盾。

items.meaningCN: 指向两个方向，因而含混

items.meaning: worth, from the same Latin valere
items.meaningCN: 价值，来自同一拉丁词 valere
items.example: The value of the gift was modest.
Patience is a state of waiting.
items.exampleCN: patience 是一种等待的状态。

definition_zh: 敌对的；对立的；相互拮抗的；怀有敌意的
definition_en: showing active opposition or hostility, or acting against another force
core_image: 两个人从门框两侧同时推同一扇门，门轴被顶得吱呀作响
scene: 谈判开始前，双方代表都不肯先坐下，措辞里各自带着刺。The two managers were openly antagonistic toward each other at the meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 antagonistic 指人与人之间明显怀有敌意（第 1 个义项：敌视他人）；句意为两位经理在会上公然地互怀敌意。

senses.title: Hostile toward a person
senses.definition: openly hostile to a particular person or group
senses.definitionCN: 对某个特定的人或群体公然敌视
senses.example: His antagonistic remarks made cooperation impossible.
senses.exampleCN: 他带有敌意的话让合作无法进行。
senses.why: The Greek word began as a contest between two fighters; when it moves into a meeting room, the same two-sided opposition remains.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词最初指两名斗士之间的较量；进入会议室后，那种两边对峙的结构仍然保留。

senses.title: Two sides pushing apart
senses.definition: acting as one of two sides whose aims push in opposite directions
senses.definitionCN: 作为两个目标相反、彼此推开的一方
senses.example: The two committees held antagonistic views on the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 两个委员会对预算持对立看法。
senses.why: A contest needs two competitors facing each other; the adjective keeps that facing posture even when the struggle is verbal.
senses.whyCN: 较量需要两名参赛者正面相对；即使斗争只是言辞上的，这个形容词仍保留那种正面对峙的姿态。

senses.title: A muscle working in opposition
senses.definition: of a muscle, pulling in the direction opposite to another muscle at the same joint
senses.definitionCN: 指肌肉在同一关节上朝与另一块肌肉相反的方向拉动
senses.example: The biceps and triceps are antagonistic muscles.
senses.exampleCN: 肱二头肌与肱三头肌是拮抗肌。
senses.why: The body needs pairs of pullers: one bends the joint, the other straightens it, so opposition is a design feature rather than a fault.
senses.whyCN: 身体需要成对的牵引者：一块弯曲关节，另一块伸直关节，因此对立是设计特性而非缺陷。

senses.title: A substance acting against another
senses.definition: of a chemical or drug, counteracting or blocking the effect of another substance
senses.definitionCN: 指化学物质或药物抵消、阻断另一物质的作用
senses.example: The drug is antagonistic to the hormone it resembles.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药物与它所仿效的激素相互拮抗。
senses.why: A molecule can fit the same receptor without activating it, so it occupies the place and blocks the partner: opposition at the smallest scale.
senses.whyCN: 分子可以占据同一受体却不激活它，于是占住位置并挡住伙伴：这是最小尺度上的对立。

senses.title: Clashing interests
senses.definition: of interests or goals, competing in a way where one side's gain is the other's loss
senses.definitionCN: 指利益或目标相争，一方所得即另一方所失
senses.example: Labor and management were not always antagonistic.
senses.exampleCN: 劳资双方并非总是利益对立。
senses.why: When two groups want the same limited thing, their positions are drawn as arrows pointing away from each other.
senses.whyCN: 当两个群体想要同一件有限之物时，它们的立场就被画成两支彼此背离的箭头。

senses.title: A hostile manner
senses.definition: expressed in a sharp, provocative or uncooperative way
senses.definitionCN: 以尖刻、挑衅或不合作的方式表达
senses.example: She answered the question in an antagonistic tone.
senses.exampleCN: 她以敌对的语气回答了这个问题。
senses.why: Tone is the surface where the inner opposition becomes audible; the word can describe the manner as well as the relation.
senses.whyCN: 语气是内在对立变得可听见的表面；这个词既可描述关系，也可描述方式。

senses.title: Competing for one resource
senses.definition: of organisms, competing for the same limited resource in an ecosystem
senses.definitionCN: 指生物在生态系统中争夺同一有限资源
senses.example: The two species are antagonistic in their feeding habits.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个物种在取食习性上相互竞争。
senses.why: Ecology borrows the contest image: two populations drawing on one food supply behave like two rivals at one table.
senses.whyCN: 生态学借用了较量意象：两个种群取用同一份食物，就像两个对手坐在同一张桌旁。

senses.title: A force against the hero
senses.definition: of a character or force in a story, standing in opposition to the protagonist
senses.definitionCN: 指故事中与主人公相对抗的人物或力量
senses.example: The novel sets an antagonistic brother against the hero.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说让一个敌对的兄弟与主人公对抗。
senses.why: Narrative needs resistance; the antagonist supplies the wall that the hero must move through.
senses.whyCN: 叙事需要阻力；反派提供那堵主人公必须穿过的墙。

intro.en: Antagonistic comes from the Greek word for a rival in a contest, built from 'against' and 'struggle'.
intro.cn: antagonistic 来自希腊语中表示「比赛对手」的词，由「反对」与「争斗」构成。

items.en: English formed antagonistic in the 17c. from antagonist, and by the 19c. it described opposed forces in politics, medicine and biology.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪由 antagonist 造出 antagonistic；到十九世纪，它已描述政治、医学与生物学中的对立力量。

items.en: Antagonistes meant 'a rival, an opponent in a contest', one who struggles against another.
items.cn: antagonistes 意为「对手、比赛中的竞争者」，即与另一人争斗的人。

items.en: The prefix anti- means 'against, in opposition to', as in antidote and antipathy.
items.cn: 前缀 anti- 意为「反对、对抗」，如 antidote 与 antipathy。

items.en: Agon meant 'contest, struggle', especially the athletic and dramatic contests of Greek festivals; it gives agony and agonize.
items.cn: agon 意为「竞赛、争斗」，尤指希腊节庆中的体育与戏剧比赛；它产生了 agony 与 agonize。

items.en: Medicine named opposing muscles and opposing drugs antagonistic, while ecology applied the word to species competing for one resource.
items.cn: 医学把相互对抗的肌肉与药物称为拮抗；生态学则用这个词指争夺同一资源的物种。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Greek contest root; the near-meaning group names forms of opposition.
note.cn: 形近组共享希腊语「竞赛」词根；近义组列出对立的各种形态。

entries.definition: a rival or opponent, especially the chief opponent in a story.
entries.definitionCN: 对手或敌手，尤指故事中的主要反对者。

entries.definition: active hostility or opposition between sides.
entries.definitionCN: 各方之间积极的敌意或对立。

entries.definition: in a hostile or opposing manner.
entries.definitionCN: 以敌对或对立的方式。

entries.definition: to suffer intense struggle or worry, from the same Greek agon.
entries.definitionCN: 承受剧烈挣扎或焦虑，来自同一个希腊词 agon。

entries.definition: treating the other side as an opponent to be defeated.
entries.definitionCN: 把对方当作必须击败的对手。

entries.definition: unfriendly and ready to attack or oppose.
entries.definitionCN: 不友好并准备攻击或反对。

entries.definition: holding a position against something or someone.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事物或某人持反对立场。

entries.definition: hostile to something and likely to damage it.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事物怀有敌意并可能损害它。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the 'against' prefix and the picture of two people at one door.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想利用「反对」前缀和「两人同推一扇门」的画面。

normal.en: anti means against, agon means contest: an antagonistic person is against you in the contest.
normal.cn: anti 意为反对，agon 意为竞赛：antagonistic 的人就是在竞赛中站到你对面的人。

normal.en: Picture two hands on one door, one on each side, both pushing inward.
normal.cn: 想象两只手分别按在门的两侧，同时往里推。

normal.en: The -ist ending names the person, the -istic ending describes the attitude.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ist 命名那个人，词尾 -istic 描述那种态度。

normal.en: Link it with protagonist: the pro is for the hero, the ant is against.
normal.cn: 把它和 protagonist 联系：pro 站在主角一边，ant 站在对面。

normal.en: Say the middle syllable as 'tagon', like two tag teams facing off.
normal.cn: 把中间音节读成 tagon，像两支接力队正面对峙。

abstract.en: Opposition can be a design feature, as with muscles that pull both ways.
abstract.cn: 对立可以是设计特性，就像朝两个方向拉动的肌肉。

abstract.en: At molecular scale, blocking a receptor is the same contest in miniature.
abstract.cn: 在分子尺度上，占据受体就是同一场较量的缩小版。

abstract.en: A story needs a wall, and the antagonist is that wall.
abstract.cn: 故事需要一堵墙，反派就是那堵墙。

examples.en: His antagonistic remarks made cooperation impossible.
examples.cn: 他带有敌意的话让合作无法进行。

examples.en: The two departments have long been antagonistic.
examples.cn: 这两个部门长期以来相互对立。

examples.en: Antagonistic muscles work in pairs to move the joint.
examples.cn: 拮抗肌成对工作以带动关节。

dict_mnemonic.text: anti（反对）+ agon（竞赛）+ istic：在竞赛里站到对面，就是「敌对的」。

root: 希腊语 antagonistes（对手）：anti-（反对）+ agon（竞赛）

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses keep the same geometry, two forces facing each other; the differences lie in whether the forces are people, muscles, molecules, interests or story roles.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留同一个几何结构，即两股力量正面相对；差别在于这两股力量是人、肌肉、分子、利益还是故事角色。

branches.en: People and groups that stand against one another.
branches.cn: 相互对立的人与群体。

branches.en: Bodies and molecules where blocking is a function, not a fault.
branches.cn: 身体与分子层面，其中阻断是功能而非缺陷。

branches.en: Interests that clash, and the tone that carries the clash.
branches.cn: 相互冲突的利益，以及承载冲突的语气。

branches.en: Species competing for one limited resource.
branches.cn: 争夺同一有限资源的物种。

branches.en: The story role that supplies resistance to the hero.
branches.cn: 为英雄提供阻力的故事角色。

intro.en: The word is a Greek prefix and root carried into English through a Latin-shaped adjective ending.
intro.cn: 这个词是希腊语前缀与词根，经拉丁式形容词词尾进入英语。

latinIntro.en: The Greek entries show the contest image that the modern word still carries.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的希腊语条目展示现代词中仍然携带的竞赛意象。

items.meaning: acting against another in a contest

items.example: The meeting ended in open antagonism.
items.exampleCN: 会议在公开敌意中结束。
她为这个选择痛苦挣扎。

items.example: The injury left him in agony.

items.exampleCN: artistic 意为具有艺术品质。

definition_zh: 涩的；收敛性的；尖刻的；严厉的
definition_en: drying and tightening to the mouth, and by extension harsh or severe in manner or effect
core_image: 咬一口未熟的柿子，整张嘴被抽干，舌面收紧发涩
scene: 评审结束前，他把稿子逐页翻过，只留下一句极短的评语。Her astringent review left little of the manuscript standing.
sceneCN: 这里 astringent 指批评言辞尖刻、不留情面（第 1 个义项：尖刻的批评）；句意为她尖刻的评论几乎把稿子批得体无完肤。

pos.zh: 涩的；收敛性的；尖刻的；严厉的

senses.title: Harshly critical in tone
senses.definition: expressed in a sharp, unsparing way that leaves little comfort
senses.definitionCN: 以尖刻、不留情面的方式表达，几乎不给人安慰
senses.example: Her astringent review left little of the manuscript standing.
senses.exampleCN: 她尖刻的评论几乎把稿子批得体无完肤。
senses.why: The physical sense of drying and tightening became a social one: words that draw the skin tight are words that allow no softness.
senses.whyCN: 物理上的「抽干、收紧」转成社会性的含义：让皮肤收紧的话，就是不留柔软余地的话。

senses.title: Drying to the mouth
senses.definition: of a substance, making the mouth feel dry and tight
senses.definitionCN: 指某物质让口腔感到干燥、紧绷
senses.example: Green bananas leave an astringent taste in the mouth.
senses.exampleCN: 青香蕉会在嘴里留下涩味。
senses.why: Tannins bind the proteins of saliva, so the mouth loses its slippery film and feels drawn tight.
senses.whyCN: 单宁与唾液蛋白结合，口腔失去滑润的薄膜，于是感觉被抽紧。

senses.title: Contracting tissue
senses.definition: causing tissues or blood vessels to contract, often to stop bleeding
senses.definitionCN: 使组织或血管收缩，常用于止血
senses.example: The nurse applied an astringent pad to the cut.
senses.exampleCN: 护士在伤口上敷了收敛性的纱布。
senses.why: Medicine uses the tightening effect directly: a surface that contracts closes small vessels and slows the flow.
senses.whyCN: 医学直接利用这种收紧作用：收缩的表面会闭合小血管、减慢血流。

senses.title: A skin toner
senses.definition: a liquid cosmetic that tightens the skin after washing
senses.definitionCN: 洗脸后用来收紧皮肤的液体化妆品
senses.example: He uses an astringent after shaving.
senses.exampleCN: 他剃须后会用收敛水。
senses.why: The same contraction moves into the bathroom: the sensation of tightened pores is sold as freshness.
senses.whyCN: 同样的收缩进入日常护理：毛孔收紧的感觉被当作清爽来出售。

senses.title: A strict economic policy
senses.definition: of policy, deliberately strict and frugal, cutting spending sharply
senses.definitionCN: 指政策刻意严苛节俭，大幅削减开支
senses.example: The astringent budget cut funds for the arts.
senses.exampleCN: 严厉的预算削减了艺术经费。
senses.why: A budget can be tightened the way tissue is tightened: less slack, less softness, a harder surface.
senses.whyCN: 预算可以像组织一样被收紧：更少余量、更少柔软、更硬的表面。

senses.title: A tightening sensation
senses.definition: a physical feeling of constriction, as if something is drawing tight
senses.definitionCN: 一种被勒紧、抽紧的身体感觉
senses.example: A cold wind gave an astringent feel to the morning air.
senses.exampleCN: 冷风让清晨的空气有一种收紧的感觉。
senses.why: Constriction is felt before it is named: cold air, a bitter taste and tight skin all report the same inward pull.
senses.whyCN: 收缩在被命名之前就被感觉到：冷空气、苦味与紧绷的皮肤都在报告同一种向内拉扯。

senses.title: Cutting wit
senses.definition: humour that is sharp and dry, often at someone's expense
senses.definitionCN: 尖锐而干燥的幽默，常以他人为代价
senses.example: His astringent wit kept the room awake and uneasy.
senses.exampleCN: 他刻薄的机智让全场既清醒又不安。
senses.why: Dry wit draws the listener tight the way tannin draws the mouth, so pleasure and discomfort arrive together.
senses.whyCN: 冷峻的机智让听者像被单宁抽紧口腔那样绷起来，快感与不适同时到达。

senses.title: A tanning agent
senses.definition: a substance used to tighten hides in leather making
senses.definitionCN: 制革时用来收紧皮张的物质
senses.example: Oak bark was long used as an astringent in tanning.
senses.exampleCN: 橡树皮长期被用作制革的收敛剂。
senses.why: Leather making uses the contraction directly: the hide shrinks and hardens around the tannin, which is the same action as a styptic on a cut.
senses.whyCN: 制革直接利用这种收缩：皮张在单宁周围收缩变硬，这与止血剂作用于伤口是同一个动作。

intro.en: Astringent comes from a Latin verb meaning 'to draw tight', the same root that gives stringent.
intro.cn: astringent 来自一个意为「抽紧」的拉丁动词，与 stringent 同根。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective in the 16c. for medicines that stop bleeding, and later extended it to taste and to severe speech.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个形容词，用于止血药物；后来扩展到味道与严厉言辞。

items.en: Astringere meant 'to draw tight, bind fast', formed from ad- 'to' and stringere 'to bind'.
items.cn: astringere 意为「抽紧、牢牢束缚」，由 ad-「向」与 stringere「束紧」构成。

items.en: Stringere 'to bind, draw tight' also gives stringent, strict and strain through related forms.
items.cn: stringere「束紧、抽紧」也通过相关形式产生 stringent、strict 与 strain。

items.en: A styptic astringent contracts small vessels; the same word names the drying mouthfeel caused by tannins.
items.cn: 止血收敛剂使小血管收缩；同一个词也命名单宁造成的口腔干燥感。

items.en: From the tightening of tissue came the tightening of tone: by the 19c. an astringent remark was one that left no room for comfort.
items.cn: 从组织的收紧衍生出语气的收紧：到十九世纪，astringent 的话已指不留安慰余地的话。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin root for binding tight; the near-meaning group names kinds of harshness.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「束紧」词根；近义组列出各种严厉。

entries.definition: the quality of being drying, tightening or severe.
entries.definitionCN: 涩、收敛或严厉的性质。

entries.definition: in a drying, tightening or sharp manner.
entries.definitionCN: 以收敛、收紧或尖刻的方式。

entries.definition: to contract or draw tight, used of tissue.
entries.definitionCN: 使收缩或抽紧，用于组织。

entries.definition: strict and precise, from the same Latin stringere.
entries.definitionCN: 严格而精确，来自同一个拉丁词 stringere。

entries.definition: unpleasantly rough, severe or cruel.
entries.definitionCN: 粗糙、严厉或残酷得令人不适。

entries.definition: bitter and cutting in tone, able to burn.
entries.definitionCN: 语气尖酸刻薄，也能指腐蚀性的。

entries.definition: serious and strict, allowing no lightness.
entries.definitionCN: 严肃严格，不容轻快。

entries.definition: able to stop bleeding by contracting tissue.
entries.definitionCN: 通过收缩组织止血的。

normalIntro.en: The hooks tie the spelling to the feeling of a mouth drawn tight.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把拼写和「嘴被抽紧」的感觉连起来。

normal.en: Think of a green banana: the tongue sticks to the roof of the mouth, and that is astringent.
normal.cn: 想想青香蕉：舌头黏在上颚，那就是 astringent 的感觉。

normal.en: The word contains string: something is pulled as tight as a string.
normal.cn: 词里有 string：某样东西被拉得像弦一样紧。

normal.en: Astringent criticism tightens the face the way tannin tightens the mouth.
normal.cn: 尖刻的批评让人的脸绷紧，就像单宁让嘴绷紧。

normal.en: Say a-STRIN-gent, with the stress on the tightening middle.
normal.cn: 读成 a-STRIN-gent，重音落在表示「收紧」的中间音节。

normal.en: Pair it with stringent: both come from the Latin verb to bind tight.
normal.cn: 把它和 stringent 配对：两个词都来自拉丁语「束紧」动词。

abstract.en: Contraction is the single mechanism behind taste, medicine and tone.
abstract.cn: 收缩是味道、医学与语气背后的同一个机制。

abstract.en: A budget with no slack feels tight in the same way a mouth does.
abstract.cn: 没有余量的预算，感觉就像被抽紧的嘴。

abstract.en: What dries also refuses softness, which is why the word can mean severe.
abstract.cn: 抽干的东西也拒绝柔软，所以这个词可以表示严厉。

examples.en: Her astringent review left little of the manuscript standing.
examples.cn: 她尖刻的评论几乎把稿子批得体无完肤。

examples.en: Green bananas leave an astringent taste in the mouth.
examples.cn: 青香蕉会在嘴里留下涩味。

examples.en: The nurse applied an astringent pad to the cut.
examples.cn: 护士在伤口上敷了收敛性的纱布。

dict_mnemonic.text: a（向）+ string（束紧）+ ent：把组织抽紧的东西，就是「收敛的、涩的」，引申为「尖刻的」。

root: 拉丁语 astringere（抽紧）：ad-（向）+ stringere（束紧）

sensesIntro.en: Astringent always describes a drawing tight; the senses differ in what is tightened, whether tissue, the mouth, a budget or a tone of voice.
sensesIntro.cn: astringent 始终描述一种「抽紧」；各义项的差别在于被抽紧的是什么，是组织、口腔、预算还是语气。

branches.en: Speech and wit that allow no softness.
branches.cn: 不容柔软的话语与机智。

branches.en: Taste and skincare, where the drying is felt on the body.
branches.cn: 味觉与护肤，其中干燥感落在身体上。

branches.en: Medical and craft uses that contract tissue or hide.
branches.cn: 收缩组织或皮张的医学与工艺用途。

branches.en: A budget tightened until no slack remains.
branches.cn: 被收紧到没有余量的预算。

branches.en: The raw sensation of constriction itself.
branches.cn: 收缩这一原始感觉本身。

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb stem with an English adjective ending, and its relatives still show the binding image.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁动词词干加英语形容词词尾，它的同族词仍显示「束紧」意象。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show how 'to bind' became 'to tighten' and then 'to be severe'.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁语条目展示「束缚」如何变成「收紧」，再变成「严厉」。

items.example: The lotion has an astringent effect.
Tannin gives the wine its astringency.
She spoke astringently of the plan.
items.exampleCN: 她尖刻地谈到这个计划。

definition_zh: 削弱；减轻；使变细；使稀薄
definition_en: to make something weaker, thinner or less intense
core_image: 一根绳子被越拉越长，绳身越来越细，最后只剩一根发亮的丝
scene: 工程师把信号在长电缆里逐段变弱的过程画成一条向下弯的曲线。Repeaters are placed along the cable so that the signal does not attenuate too quickly.
sceneCN: 这里 attenuate 指信号强度沿线路逐渐减弱（第 1 个义项：强度减弱）；句意为电缆沿线设置中继器，以免信号衰减过快。

senses.title: Reduce intensity
senses.definition: to make a force, effect or feeling weaker
senses.definitionCN: 使力量、效果或感受变弱
senses.example: Thick walls attenuate the sound of the traffic.
senses.exampleCN: 厚墙削弱了交通的声响。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to make thin': a strong thing is drawn out until it has less body, and less body means less force.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「使变薄」：强的东西被拉长到body更少，而更少的分量就意味着更小的力量。

senses.title: Signal loss along a path
senses.definition: to reduce the strength of an electrical or acoustic signal
senses.definitionCN: 降低电信号或声信号的强度
senses.example: The cable attenuates the signal over long distances.
senses.exampleCN: 电缆在长距离上削弱信号。
senses.why: A signal is a wave carrying energy; as the wave spreads, the same energy covers more space and each point receives less.
senses.whyCN: 信号是携带动能的波；波扩散时同样的能量覆盖更大空间，每一点接收到的就更少。

senses.title: Make thin or tapered
senses.definition: to make something slender, or to draw it out until it narrows
senses.definitionCN: 使某物变细长，或把它拉长到逐渐变窄
senses.example: The glassblower attenuated the neck of the flask.
senses.exampleCN: 吹玻璃的工匠把瓶颈拉细。
senses.why: This is the oldest physical sense: the object keeps its material but loses its thickness.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的物理义：物体保留材质，却失去厚度。

senses.title: Weaken a pathogen
senses.definition: to reduce the virulence of a microorganism so it can be used in a vaccine
senses.definitionCN: 降低微生物的毒性，使其可用于疫苗
senses.example: Scientists attenuated the virus to make a safe vaccine.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家使病毒减毒，以制造安全的疫苗。
senses.why: A virus that has lost its sharp edge can still teach the body its shape without causing the disease.
senses.whyCN: 失去锋芒的病毒仍能让身体记住它的形状，却不会引发疾病。

senses.title: Make a sound fainter
senses.definition: to reduce the volume or clarity of a sound
senses.definitionCN: 降低声音的音量或清晰度
senses.example: Heavy curtains attenuated the music from the street.
senses.exampleCN: 厚重的窗帘减弱了街上的音乐声。
senses.why: Sound is a pressure wave; a heavy curtain absorbs part of the energy, so the wave arrives with less push.
senses.whyCN: 声音是压力波；厚重窗帘吸收部分能量，因此波到达时推力更小。

senses.title: Water down an idea
senses.definition: to make a statement, argument or proposal less forceful
senses.definitionCN: 使陈述、论证或提议的力度变小
senses.example: The lawyer tried to attenuate the impact of the confession.
senses.exampleCN: 律师试图减弱这份供词的影响。
senses.why: An argument is strength of claim; to attenuate it is to draw the claim thin until it no longer presses.
senses.whyCN: 论证就是主张的力度；削弱它就是把它抽薄，直到不再压人。

senses.title: Reduce risk or harm
senses.definition: to lower the likelihood or severity of harm
senses.definitionCN: 降低伤害发生的可能或严重程度
senses.example: Early warning systems attenuate the damage of storms.
senses.exampleCN: 早期预警系统减轻风暴造成的损失。
senses.why: A warning acts before the event, so it removes some of the energy that the harm would otherwise carry.
senses.whyCN: 预警在事件之前起作用，因此它移除了伤害原本会携带的一部分能量。

senses.title: Fade with distance
senses.definition: to become weaker as it spreads through a medium
senses.definitionCN: 在介质中扩散时逐渐变弱
senses.example: The scent attenuated as we walked away from the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 我们离开花园后，香气渐渐变淡。
senses.why: A scent is particles spreading outward; the further they spread, the fewer reach any one point.
senses.whyCN: 气味是向外扩散的微粒；扩散得越远，到达任一点的就越多。

intro.en: Attenuate is built from a Latin verb for thinning, and the same root gives tenuous.
intro.cn: attenuate 由一个意为「使变薄」的拉丁动词构成，同一个词根产生了 tenuous。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the 16c. for making things thin, and modern technical writing uses it for signals, risks and vaccines.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个动词，表示使变薄；现代技术文本用它指信号、风险与疫苗。

items.en: Attenuare meant 'to make thin, lessen, weaken', formed from ad- 'to' and tenuis 'thin'.
items.cn: attenuare 意为「使变薄、减少、削弱」，由 ad-「向」与 tenuis「薄」构成。

items.en: Tenuis meant 'thin, fine, slight', and also gave English tenuous and the musical term tenor through related forms.
items.cn: tenuis 意为「薄、细、轻微」，也通过相关形式产生英语 tenuous 与音乐术语 tenor。

items.en: Physics measures attenuation in decibels; medicine attenuates pathogens to produce live vaccines.
items.cn: 物理学用分贝衡量衰减；医学使病原体减毒以生产活疫苗。

items.en: The physical image of thinning became an abstract one: claims, risks and feelings can all be drawn thin.
items.cn: 「变薄」的物理形象变成抽象形象：主张、风险与情感都可以被抽薄。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the thinning root or the same derived forms; the near-meaning group names ways of making something less.
note.cn: 形近组共享「变薄」词根或同一派生形式；近义组列出使某物变小的各种方式。

entries.definitionCN: 削弱或变细的行为或程度。

entries.definition: weakened, especially of a virus used in a vaccine.
entries.definitionCN: 被削弱的，尤指疫苗中所用的病毒。

entries.definition: a device that reduces signal strength.
entries.definitionCN: 降低信号强度的装置。

entries.definition: thin, slight and weak, from the same Latin tenuis.

entries.definition: to make or become smaller in size or importance.

entries.definition: to make a liquid weaker by adding water or another fluid.
entries.definitionCN: 加水或其他液体使液体变淡。

entries.definition: to make something harmful less severe.
entries.definitionCN: 使有害之事不那么严重。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a thing drawn thin until its force drops.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把「东西被抽薄直到力量下降」的画面留住。

normal.en: Think tenuis, Latin for thin: attenuate means to make thin in body or force.
normal.cn: 想想拉丁语 tenuis「薄」：attenuate 就是让实体或力量变薄。

normal.en: Picture a rope pulled longer and longer until it is a thread.
normal.cn: 想象一根绳子被越拉越长，最后成了一根细线。

normal.en: A signal that fades along a cable is being attenuated by the cable itself.
normal.cn: 沿电缆逐渐变弱的信号，正是被电缆本身衰减。

normal.en: A vaccine virus is attenuated: it keeps the shape but loses the sting.
normal.cn: 疫苗里的病毒是减毒的：保留形状，失去刺痛。

normal.en: Say the word as at-TEN-u-ate, with the thin root in the middle.
normal.cn: 读成 at-TEN-u-ate，中间正是「薄」的词根。

abstract.en: Less body means less force, whether the body is a rope, a wave or a claim.
abstract.cn: 实体更少就意味着力量更小，无论这个实体是绳子、波还是主张。

abstract.en: Reducing a risk works like thinning a wave before it reaches the shore.
abstract.cn: 降低风险就像在波浪抵达岸边之前把它削薄。

abstract.en: What is attenuated still exists, only with less power to act.
abstract.cn: 被削弱之物仍然存在，只是行动的力量更小。

examples.cn: 厚墙削弱了交通的声响。

examples.en: Scientists attenuated the virus to make a safe vaccine.
examples.cn: 科学家使病毒减毒，以制造安全的疫苗。

examples.en: The lawyer tried to attenuate the impact of the confession.

dict_mnemonic.text: at（向）+ tenu（薄）+ ate（动词）：把东西抽薄，就是「削弱、减轻」。

root: 拉丁语 attenuare（使变薄）：ad-（向）+ tenuis（薄）

sensesIntro.en: Attenuate always reduces body or force; the senses differ in what is being thinned, from glass and signals to viruses, arguments and risks.
sensesIntro.cn: attenuate 始终是让实体或力量变少；各义项的差别在于被抽薄的对象，从玻璃与信号到病毒、论证与风险。

branches.en: Sound and general force made weaker.
branches.cn: 被减弱的声音与一般力量。

branches.en: Waves and scents that lose strength as they spread.
branches.cn: 扩散时失去强度的波与气味。

branches.en: The oldest physical sense, drawing a material thin.

branches.en: Viruses and risks reduced on purpose, for safety.
branches.cn: 为安全而刻意降低的病毒与风险。

branches.en: Claims and arguments drawn thin until they stop pressing.
branches.cn: 被抽薄到不再压人的主张与论证。

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb stem with an English verb ending, and its family keeps the image of thinness.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁动词词干加英语动词词尾，它的同族词都保留「薄」的形象。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show how thinness became weakness and then reduction of every kind.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁语条目展示「薄」如何变成「弱」，再变成各种意义的减少。

definition_zh: 磨损；消耗；人员自然减员；逐步削弱
definition_en: a gradual wearing down or reduction, whether of material, people or strength
core_image: 两块石头在水流里互相摩擦，棱角一年年变小，最后只剩光滑的卵石
scene: 项目组没有裁员，只是不再补缺，两年后办公室里少了三分之一的人。The company managed the decline by attrition rather than layoffs.
sceneCN: 这里 attrition 指靠不补缺实现的人员自然减员（第 2 个义项：自然减员）；句意为公司靠自然减员而不是裁员来应对规模缩减。

pos.zh: 磨损；消耗；自然减员；逐步削弱

senses.title: Wearing away by friction
senses.definition: the gradual wearing away of a surface by continuous rubbing
senses.definitionCN: 表面因持续摩擦而逐渐损耗
senses.example: The tyres showed heavy attrition after two seasons.
senses.exampleCN: 两个赛季之后，轮胎磨损严重。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to rub against'; the noun names what rubbing leaves behind, a surface slowly losing its material.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「相互摩擦」；名词命名摩擦留下的结果，即表面慢慢失去材质。

senses.title: Natural staff reduction
senses.definition: a decrease in staff numbers achieved by not replacing those who leave
senses.definitionCN: 不补替离职者，从而实现员工人数下降
senses.example: The firm reduced its payroll through attrition.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司靠自然减员来缩减人员开支。
senses.why: People leave for their own reasons; if no one replaces them, the group shrinks without a single dismissal, which is a quiet form of wearing down.
senses.whyCN: 人们因自己的原因离开；若不补人，团队就在没有一次解雇的情况下缩小，这是一种安静的消耗。

senses.title: Gradual weakening
senses.definition: a slow loss of strength, morale or numbers under sustained pressure
senses.definitionCN: 在持续压力下力量、士气或人数的缓慢流失
senses.example: The long campaign caused serious attrition in the ranks.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长的战役让队伍严重损耗。
senses.why: Morale is also a material: every small setback takes a little away, and no single defeat is responsible for the total.
senses.whyCN: 士气也是一种材料：每次小挫折都带走一点，总量不由任何一次失败单独负责。

senses.title: A war of attrition
senses.definition: a conflict in which each side tries to exhaust the other rather than win a decisive battle
senses.definitionCN: 各方试图耗尽对方而非争取决定性胜利的冲突
senses.example: The border dispute became a war of attrition.
senses.exampleCN: 这场边境争端变成了一场消耗战。
senses.why: When neither side can strike a finish, the aim shifts from beating the enemy to making the enemy spend more than it can replace.
senses.whyCN: 当双方都无法一击定局时，目标就从打败敌人转为让敌人消耗超过其补充能力。

senses.title: Loss of members or customers
senses.definition: the gradual loss of members, customers or students over time
senses.definitionCN: 成员、客户或学生随时间逐渐流失
senses.example: The gym's attrition rate worried its owners.
senses.exampleCN: 这家健身房的会员流失率让老板担忧。
senses.why: Members leave one at a time for ordinary reasons; the total loss is visible only in the rate.
senses.whyCN: 成员因日常原因一个一个离开；总损失只能从流失率上看见。

senses.title: Rock erosion
senses.definition: the grinding down of rock fragments by water, wind or ice
senses.definitionCN: 岩石碎片被水、风或冰磨小
senses.example: River pebbles are shaped by decades of attrition.
senses.exampleCN: 河里的卵石是数十年磨蚀塑成的。
senses.why: Water carries sand that acts as grit, so the stone is rubbed by the load it travels with.
senses.whyCN: 水流携带沙砾作为磨料，于是石头被同行的负载磨小。

senses.title: Theological attrition
senses.titleCN: 神学意义上的「下等痛悔」
senses.definition: in theology, sorrow for sin caused by fear of punishment rather than by love of God
senses.definitionCN: 在神学中，因害怕惩罚而非因爱上帝产生的悔罪
senses.example: The old manual distinguishes attrition from contrition.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时的手册把下等痛悔与上等痛悔区分开来。
senses.why: Theological writing borrowed the wear image: fear rubs the will down without changing its love.
senses.whyCN: 神学写作借用了磨损意象：恐惧磨低意志，却不改变它的爱。

senses.title: Wear from sustained use
senses.definition: the slow decline of equipment or material through ordinary use
senses.definitionCN: 设备或材料因日常使用而缓慢退化
senses.example: The museum limited handling because of attrition to the binding.
senses.exampleCN: 由于装帧不断损耗，博物馆限制了翻阅。
senses.why: Every use removes a little material; the noun measures that total loss rather than any single break.
senses.whyCN: 每次使用都带走一点材料；这个名词衡量的是总损失，而不是某一次断裂。

intro.en: Attrition comes from a Latin verb meaning 'to rub against', the same root family as trite and detritus.
intro.cn: attrition 来自一个意为「相互摩擦」的拉丁动词，与 trite、detritus 同属一个词根家族。

items.en: English took the noun in the 15c. for rubbing or friction, and later used it for staff loss and for exhausting wars.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个名词，表示摩擦；后来用于人员流失与消耗战。

items.en: Attritio meant 'a rubbing against, friction, wear', the noun of action from atterere.
items.cn: attritio 意为「摩擦、磨损」，是 atterere 的动作名词。

items.en: Atterere 'to rub against, wear down' is ad- 'to' plus terere 'to rub'.
items.cn: atterere「摩擦、磨掉」由 ad-「向」与 terere「摩擦」构成。

items.en: Terere 'to rub' also gives trite, originally 'rubbed smooth', and detritus, the material rubbed away.
items.cn: terere「摩擦」也产生 trite（原意「被磨平」）与 detritus（被磨掉的碎屑）。

items.en: The idea of material rubbed away became the idea of people or strength quietly drained, especially in business and military writing.
items.cn: 材料被磨掉的概念，变成人员或力量被悄然耗尽的概念，在商业与军事文本中尤其常见。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the rubbing root; the near-meaning group names ways of being worn down or drained.
note.cn: 形近组共享「摩擦」词根；近义组列出被磨耗或耗尽的各种方式。

entries.definition: relating to wearing down or gradual loss.
entries.definitionCN: 与磨损或逐步流失有关。

entries.definition: to wear down or reduce gradually.
entries.definitionCN: 逐步磨损或削减。

entries.definition: deep sorrow for wrongdoing, from the same Latin terere.
entries.definitionCN: 对过错的深切悔恨，来自同一拉丁词 terere。

entries.definition: debris worn away from a larger mass.
entries.definitionCN: 从大块物质上磨掉的碎屑。

entries.definition: the gradual wearing away of rock or soil.
entries.definitionCN: 岩石或土壤逐渐被磨去。

entries.definition: damage caused by continuous use or friction.
entries.definitionCN: 持续使用或摩擦造成的损伤。

entries.definition: the reduction of a resource until little remains.
entries.definitionCN: 资源被消耗到所剩无几。

entries.definition: loss of employees, students or materials that could have been used.
entries.definitionCN: 本可利用的员工、学生或材料的损失。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of two stones grinding each other smaller.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把「两块石头互相磨小」的画面留住。

normal.en: Think of tri, to rub: attrition is the result of steady rubbing.
normal.cn: 想想词根 terere「摩擦」：attrition 就是持续摩擦的结果。

normal.en: Picture two river stones knocking together until the corners are gone.
normal.cn: 想象两块河石不断相撞，直到棱角消失。

normal.en: A company that does not replace leavers is worn down the same way.
normal.cn: 不补替离职者的公司，也是以同样的方式被磨小。

normal.en: In a war of attrition, the goal is not to win but to outlast.
normal.cn: 在消耗战中，目标不是取胜，而是撑得比对方久。

normal.en: Say at-TRI-tion, with the rubbing root stressed in the middle.
normal.cn: 读成 at-TRI-tion，重音落在表示「摩擦」的词根上。

abstract.en: No single blow explains the loss; the total comes from repetition.
abstract.cn: 没有哪一次打击能解释全部损失；总量来自重复。

abstract.en: People are a resource that can be drained quietly, without a dismissal.
abstract.cn: 人是一种可以被安静耗尽的资源，不必经过解雇。

abstract.en: What remains after attrition is smooth, smaller and easier to overlook.
abstract.cn: 磨耗之后剩下的东西更光滑、更小，也更容易被忽视。

examples.en: The tyres showed heavy attrition after two seasons.
examples.cn: 两个赛季之后，轮胎磨损严重。

examples.en: The firm reduced its payroll through attrition.
examples.cn: 这家公司靠自然减员来缩减人员开支。

examples.en: The border dispute became a war of attrition.
examples.cn: 这场边境争端变成了一场消耗战。

dict_mnemonic.text: at（向）+ trit（摩擦）+ ion（名词）：不断相互摩擦，就是「磨损、消耗」。

root: 拉丁语 attritio（摩擦），源自 atterere：ad-（向）+ terere（摩擦）

sensesIntro.en: Attrition is always loss by repetition rather than by one blow; the senses differ in whether the material lost is stone, rubber, staff, morale or customers.
sensesIntro.cn: attrition 始终是「重复造成的损失」而非一次打击；各义项的差别在于失去的材料是石头、橡胶、员工、士气还是客户。

branches.en: Stone, rubber and surfaces worn by friction.
branches.cn: 被摩擦磨损的石头、橡胶与表面。

branches.en: People and members lost by not replacing them.
branches.cn: 因不补替而流失的员工与成员。

branches.en: The general decline of strength or morale.
branches.cn: 力量或士气的普遍下滑。

branches.en: The strategy that aims to exhaust rather than defeat.
branches.cn: 旨在耗尽而非击败的战略。

branches.en: The old theological sense, and loss through ordinary use.
branches.cn: 古老的神学义，以及日常使用造成的损耗。

intro.en: The word is a Latin noun of action on a verb meaning to rub, with English relatives that keep the same image.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「摩擦」动词的动作名词，其英语同族词保留同一意象。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show rubbing becoming friction, then wear, then quiet depletion.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁语条目展示「摩擦」如何变成「磨损」，再变成「悄然耗尽」。

items.exampleCN: 人员损耗已经削减了团队。

definition_zh: 朴素的；严峻的；苦行的；简朴无饰的
definition_en: deliberately plain and without ornament, or strict and severe in manner or conditions
core_image: 一间石屋，只有木桌、木凳和一盏灯，墙面空得能听见回声
scene: 山中的小屋只有一张木桌、一盏灯，墙上没有任何装饰。The monks live an austere life with few possessions.
sceneCN: 这里 austere 指生活朴素、没有装饰与奢侈品（第 1 个义项：朴素无饰）；句意为僧侣们过着几乎没有财物的简朴生活。

senses.title: Plain and without ornament
senses.definition: deliberately simple, with no decoration and no unnecessary comfort
senses.definitionCN: 刻意简单，没有装饰，也没有多余的舒适
senses.example: The monks live an austere life with few possessions.
senses.exampleCN: 僧侣们过着几乎没有财物的简朴生活。
senses.why: The Greek word meant 'dry, harsh': anything stripped of moisture is also stripped of softness, and a room can be described the same way.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词意为「干燥、粗硬」：被抽去水分的东西也被抽去柔软，房间也可以用同样的方式描述。

senses.title: Severe in manner
senses.definition: strict and serious in manner, allowing no warmth or lightness
senses.definitionCN: 举止严格而严肃，不容温暖或轻快
senses.example: The headmaster gave an austere welcome and then listed the rules.
senses.exampleCN: 校长作了严峻的欢迎，随后列出各项规定。
senses.why: A person who refuses ornament in a room often refuses it in behaviour too, so plainness becomes a social style.
senses.whyCN: 一个在房间里拒绝装饰的人，往往在行为上也拒绝装饰，于是朴素变成一种社交风格。

senses.title: Morally strict
senses.definition: holding to a disciplined moral code, often with a religious basis
senses.definitionCN: 恪守严格纪律化的道德准则，常带宗教基础
senses.example: The order was known for its austere discipline.
senses.exampleCN: 这个修会以严苛的戒律闻名。
senses.why: Moral strictness borrows the image of a bare room: fewer comforts are believed to leave more attention for what matters.
senses.whyCN: 道德严格借用了空房间的意象：更少的舒适被认为能给要紧之事留下更多注意力。

senses.title: A bare place
senses.definition: of a place, cold, bare and lacking in softness or colour
senses.definitionCN: 指场所冷清、空旷，缺少柔软与色彩
senses.example: The hospital corridor was austere and brightly lit.
senses.exampleCN: 医院的走廊空荡冷清，灯光明亮。
senses.why: Architecture uses the word for spaces that refuse to comfort the body, so the eye finds nowhere soft to rest.
senses.whyCN: 建筑学用这个词指拒绝让身体舒适的空间，于是目光找不到柔软之处停留。

senses.title: Harshly restrictive policy
senses.definition: of economic policy, harshly restrictive, cutting spending and comfort
senses.definitionCN: 指经济政策严厉受限，削减开支与福利
senses.example: The government adopted austere measures after the crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 危机之后政府采取了紧缩措施。
senses.why: A national budget can be stripped the way a room is stripped: the ornaments go first, then the necessities are questioned.
senses.whyCN: 国家预算可以像房间一样被清空：先去掉装饰，接着连必需品也受到质疑。

senses.title: A restrained style
senses.definition: of art, music or writing, stripped of ornament and easy emotion
senses.definitionCN: 指艺术、音乐或写作去掉装饰与轻易的情感
senses.example: Her austere prose leaves every word exposed.
senses.exampleCN: 她克制的文笔让每个词都裸露在外。
senses.why: Style can practise the same denial as a room: what is removed makes the remaining shapes more visible.
senses.whyCN: 风格可以像房间一样实践这种舍弃：被移走的东西让剩下的形状更显眼。

senses.title: Beauty from bareness
senses.definition: a beauty that comes from bareness and proportion rather than decoration
senses.definitionCN: 源于空净与比例而非装饰的美
senses.example: The chapel is admired for its austere beauty.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小教堂以其素净之美受人赞赏。
senses.why: When ornament is gone, proportion must carry the whole effect, and that is the beauty the word praises.
senses.whyCN: 装饰消失后，比例必须承担全部效果，这正是这个词所赞赏的美。

senses.title: Deliberate self-denial
senses.definition: the practice of denying oneself comfort or pleasure for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为某个目的而刻意放弃舒适或享乐的做法
senses.example: His austerity was a protest against wasteful display.
senses.exampleCN: 他的自我节制是对铺张炫耀的一种抗议。
senses.why: Self-denial turns plainness into a choice: the bare room is not a lack but a statement.
senses.whyCN: 自我节制把朴素变成选择：空房间不是匮乏，而是一种声明。

intro.en: Austere goes back to a Greek word for dry and harsh, and entered English through Latin.
intro.cn: austere 可追溯到希腊语中表示「干燥、粗硬」的词，经拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective in the 14c. for harsh taste and strict life, and later applied it to art and architecture.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入这个形容词，用于粗涩的味道与严格的生活，后来扩展到艺术与建筑。

items.en: Latin austerus meant 'harsh, dry, sour', a loan from Greek describing things that pucker the mouth.
items.cn: 拉丁语 austerus 意为「粗硬、干燥、酸涩」，借自希腊语，描述让嘴收缩的东西。

items.en: Greek austeros meant 'dry, harsh', used of wind, taste and character alike.
items.cn: 希腊语 austeros 意为「干燥、粗硬」，风、味道与性格都可以用它形容。

items.en: The root behind austeros is connected with dryness, the same idea that makes a dry thing stiff and unbending.
items.cn: austeros 背后的词根与「干燥」有关，正是干燥使东西僵硬、不易弯曲。

items.en: In modern politics austerity names cuts in public spending, while in art it praises work stripped of ornament.
items.cn: 在现代政治中，austerity 指削减公共开支；在艺术中，它赞赏去掉装饰的作品。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the same stem; the near-meaning group names other kinds of plainness and severity.
note.cn: 形近组共享同一词干；近义组列出其他形式的朴素与严峻。

entries.definition: in a plain or severe manner.

entries.definition: very strict or harsh, without gentleness.

entries.definition: simple and harsh, allowing no luxury.
entries.definitionCN: 简单严苛，不容奢侈。

entries.definition: plain and harsh in appearance, with no softening detail.
entries.definitionCN: 外观朴素严酷，没有柔化细节。

entries.definition: careful with money and resources, avoiding waste.
entries.definitionCN: 节省金钱与资源，避免浪费。

normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把「只有一盏灯的空房间」这一画面留住。

normal.en: Picture a stone room with one table and one lamp; the missing furniture is the word.
normal.cn: 想象一间石屋，只有一桌一灯；缺席的家具就是这个词。

normal.en: Austere and 'austerity' share a stem: both mean cutting away the extra.
normal.cn: austere 与 austerity 同词干：两者都表示把多余的东西切掉。

normal.en: Dryness makes a thing stiff; a dry style is stiff and unbending too.
normal.cn: 干燥使东西僵硬；干燥的风格也僵硬而不弯。

normal.en: Say aw-STEER, as if steering away from comfort.
normal.cn: 读成 aw-STEER，好像在把方向转离舒适。

normal.en: Link it with spartan: both describe lives with few possessions.
normal.cn: 把它和 spartan 联系：两者都描述财物很少的生活。

abstract.en: Removing ornament forces proportion to carry the beauty.
abstract.cn: 去掉装饰后，比例必须承担美感。

abstract.en: A bare room can be a statement rather than a lack.
abstract.cn: 空房间可以是声明，而不只是匮乏。

abstract.en: The same word serves art, architecture and national budgets because all three can be stripped.
abstract.cn: 同一个词适用于艺术、建筑与国家预算，因为三者都可以被剥净。

examples.en: The monks live an austere life with few possessions.
examples.cn: 僧侣们过着几乎没有财物的简朴生活。

examples.en: The government adopted austere measures after the crisis.
examples.cn: 危机之后政府采取了紧缩措施。

examples.en: The chapel is admired for its austere beauty.
examples.cn: 这座小教堂以其素净之美受人赞赏。

sensesIntro.en: Austere always means something has been stripped away; the senses differ in whether what is removed is ornament, comfort, spending or softness of manner.
sensesIntro.cn: austere 始终表示某物被剥去了一层；各义项的差别在于被去掉的是装饰、舒适、开支还是举止中的柔软。
