definition_zh: 仁慈的；善意的；乐善好施的；宽厚的
definition_en: kind and generous, wishing good for others and often acting on that wish
core_image: 一位老人把自家菜园里的菜分成小份，逐户放在邻居门口，然后悄悄离开
scene: 老人把自家的菜分给巷子里每户人家，从不提回报。The benevolent teacher stayed after class to help the weakest students.
sceneCN: 这里 benevolent 指待人心怀善意、乐于给予（第 1 个义项：善意待人）；句意为这位仁慈的老师课后留下来帮助最弱的学生。

pos.zh: 仁慈的；善意的；乐善好施的

senses.title: Kind and wishing well
senses.definition: kind, generous and wishing good for other people
senses.definitionCN: 善良、慷慨，并希望他人过得好
senses.example: The benevolent teacher stayed after class to help the weakest students.
senses.exampleCN: 这位仁慈的老师课后留下来帮助最弱的学生。
senses.why: The Latin word is built from 'well' and 'to wish': benevolence is literally a good wish directed at someone.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词由「好」与「愿望」构成：仁慈字面上就是朝向某人的美好祝愿。

senses.title: Power used for others' good
senses.definition: of a ruler or authority, using power for the welfare of those under it
senses.definitionCN: 指统治者或权威把权力用于治下之人的福祉
senses.example: The benevolent ruler lowered taxes during the famine.
senses.exampleCN: 这位宽厚的统治者在饥荒期间减税。
senses.why: Power normally flows downward; when the word is attached to a ruler, it claims the flow is turned to benefit the ruled.
senses.whyCN: 权力通常自上而下流动；当这个词用于统治者时，它声称这股流向被转向了被统治者。

senses.title: Organized charity
senses.definition: of a fund or society, set up to give aid to those in need
senses.definitionCN: 指为帮助有需要者而设立的基金或团体
senses.example: A benevolent fund covered the family's medical costs.
senses.exampleCN: 一项慈善基金承担了这个家庭的医疗费用。
senses.why: The good wish becomes an institution: money is collected and distributed by rule rather than by impulse.
senses.whyCN: 美好的祝愿变成制度：钱按规则收集与分发，而不是凭一时冲动。

senses.title: A kindly expression
senses.definition: of a look or smile, expressing kindly goodwill
senses.definitionCN: 指神情或微笑流露出善意的温和
senses.example: She gave the child a benevolent smile.
senses.exampleCN: 她对孩子露出慈祥的微笑。
senses.why: A face is the smallest place where the wish becomes visible; a slight softening of the eyes reports the inner direction.
senses.whyCN: 脸是愿望变得可见的最小场所；眼神略微放软就报告了内在的朝向。

senses.title: A mutual aid association
senses.definition: a society formed so that members help one another in difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 为成员在困难时互相帮助而组成的团体
senses.example: The miners' benevolent society paid for funerals.
senses.exampleCN: 矿工的互助会承担丧葬费用。
senses.why: When people cannot rely on the state, they pool risk among themselves, and the good wish becomes a contract of mutual help.
senses.whyCN: 当人们无法依赖国家时，就在彼此之间分摊风险，美好的祝愿变成了互助的契约。

senses.title: A kindly reading of others
senses.definition: in psychology, the tendency to interpret others' actions as well meant
senses.definitionCN: 在心理学中，倾向于把他人的行为解释为出于好意
senses.example: A benevolent attribution reduces conflict in a team.
senses.exampleCN: 善意的归因能减少团队中的冲突。
senses.why: Interpretation is a choice between suspicion and goodwill; the word names the choice that assumes the better motive.
senses.whyCN: 解读是在猜疑与善意之间的选择；这个词命名那个假定较好动机的选择。

senses.title: A god disposed to good
senses.definition: in theology, of a deity, disposed toward human welfare
senses.definitionCN: 在神学中，指神对人类福祉怀有善意
senses.example: The hymn praises a benevolent creator.
senses.exampleCN: 这首赞美诗称颂慈悲的造物主。
senses.why: The same wish is projected onto the largest power imaginable, and the universe is described as friendly rather than indifferent.
senses.whyCN: 同样的愿望被投射到可想象的最大力量上，宇宙于是被描述为友善而非冷漠。

senses.title: An authoritarian with good intentions
senses.definition: in politics, an absolute ruler who claims to act for the subjects' welfare
senses.definitionCN: 在政治学中，指声称替被统治者谋福利的绝对统治者
senses.example: The essay examines the limits of benevolent dictatorship.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章探讨开明专制的局限。
senses.why: Good intentions do not change where the decision sits: the word can describe kindness without granting the ruled any say.
senses.whyCN: 善意并不改变决定所在的位置：这个词可以描述仁慈，却不给被统治者任何发言权。

intro.en: Benevolent is a Latin compound meaning 'wishing well', built from bene and velle.
intro.cn: benevolent 是一个拉丁语复合词，意为「祝愿良好」，由 bene 与 velle 构成。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective in the 15c. from Latin, first for generous patrons and later for kindly feeling in general.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪从拉丁语借入这个形容词，最初指慷慨的资助者，后来泛指善意的情感。

items.en: The Latin phrase bene velle meant 'to wish well', and the adjective benevolens named one who wishes well.
items.cn: 拉丁短语 bene velle 意为「祝愿良好」，形容词 benevolens 命名祝愿良好的人。

items.en: Bene 'well' is the adverb of bonus 'good', and appears in benefit, benediction and benefactor.
items.cn: bene「好地」是 bonus「好」的副词形式，出现于 benefit、benediction 与 benefactor 中。

items.en: Velle 'to wish, to be willing' gives voluntary and volunteer, so the wish and the willingness share one root.
items.cn: velle「愿望、愿意」产生 voluntary 与 volunteer，因此愿望与意愿共享一个词根。

items.en: The word moved from personal feeling to institutions: benevolent funds and societies made the good wish into an organized practice.
items.cn: 这个词从个人情感转向制度：慈善基金与互助会把美好的愿望变成有组织的实践。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin bene; the near-meaning group names kinds of kindness.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语 bene；近义组列出各种善意。

entries.definition: kindness and goodwill toward others.
entries.definitionCN: 对他人的善意与好心。

entries.definition: in a kind and well-wishing manner.
entries.definitionCN: 以仁慈而善意的方式。

entries.definition: doing good, active in charity.
entries.definitionCN: 行善的，积极从事慈善的。

entries.definition: a good or advantage given to someone.
entries.definitionCN: 给予某人的好处或利益。

entries.definition: showing care and goodwill toward others.
entries.definitionCN: 对他人表现出关心与善意。

entries.definition: generous in giving help, or inclined to judge others kindly.
entries.definitionCN: 乐于给予帮助，或倾向善意评判他人。

entries.definition: willing to give more than is expected.
entries.definitionCN: 愿意给出超过预期的东西。

entries.definition: kindly and not harmful in effect.
entries.definitionCN: 和善且在效果上无害。

normalIntro.en: The hooks split the word into 'well' and 'wish'.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把单词拆成「好」与「祝愿」两部分。

normal.en: bene means well, velle means wish: benevolent is wishing someone well.
normal.cn: bene 意为好，velle 意为祝愿：benevolent 就是祝人安好。

normal.en: Picture vegetables left at a neighbour's door with no note.
normal.cn: 想象把蔬菜放在邻居门口，不留字条。

normal.en: The -ent ending makes it an adjective describing a person's direction toward others.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ent 使它成为描述一个人朝向他人的形容词。

normal.en: Pair it with benefit: both begin with bene, both are about good.
normal.cn: 把它和 benefit 配对：两者都以 bene 开头，都与「好」有关。

normal.en: Say bene-violent? No: say benev-olent, and hear the soft wish inside.
normal.cn: 别读成 bene-violent：读成 benev-olent，听见里面柔软的祝愿。

abstract.en: A wish is invisible until it becomes a fund, a society or a smile.
abstract.cn: 愿望在被变成基金、团体或微笑之前是看不见的。

abstract.en: Kind intentions do not change who holds the power.
abstract.cn: 善意的意图并不改变谁掌握权力。

abstract.en: To read others benevolently is to choose the better motive when both are possible.
abstract.cn: 善意地解读他人，就是在两种动机都可能时选择较好的那一个。

examples.en: The benevolent teacher stayed after class to help the weakest students.
examples.cn: 这位仁慈的老师课后留下来帮助最弱的学生。

examples.en: A benevolent fund covered the family's medical costs.
examples.cn: 一项慈善基金承担了这个家庭的医疗费用。

examples.en: The essay examines the limits of benevolent dictatorship.
examples.cn: 这篇文章探讨开明专制的局限。

dict_mnemonic.text: bene（好）+ vol（意愿）+ ent：怀着祝人安好的意愿，就是「仁慈的」。

root: 拉丁语 benevolens：bene（好）+ velle（愿望、愿意）

sensesIntro.en: Benevolent always describes a good wish turned outward; the senses differ in whether the wish stays a feeling, becomes a smile, a fund, an institution or a claim about power.
sensesIntro.cn: benevolent 始终描述一种朝向他人的美好愿望；各义项的差别在于这愿望停留在感受、变成微笑、基金、制度，还是变成关于权力的主张。

branches.en: The feeling itself and the face that shows it.
branches.cn: 感受本身以及显露它的脸。

branches.en: Power that claims to act for the ruled, and its limits.
branches.cn: 声称替被统治者行事的权力及其局限。

branches.en: Money and mutual aid organized into institutions.
branches.cn: 被组织成制度的金钱与互助。

branches.en: The psychological habit of assuming the better motive.
branches.cn: 假定较好动机的心理习惯。

branches.en: The same wish projected onto a deity.
branches.cn: 同样的愿望被投射到神身上。

intro.en: The word is a Latin compound of an adverb and a verb, carried into English with an adjective ending.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语副词与动词的复合，加英语形容词词尾进入英语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show how 'well' and 'wish' combine into one moral word.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁语条目展示「好」与「愿望」如何合成一个道德词。

items.exampleCN: 一位仁慈的捐赠者付了病床钱。

items.example: A beneficent foundation funded the school.
items.exampleCN: 一个行善的基金会资助了这所学校。

items.example: The road brought benefit to the village.
items.exampleCN: 这条路给村子带来好处。

items.meaningCN: 自愿的，出于自己的意愿

definition_en: to support or strengthen something, or a long cushion used as a prop
core_image: 一根木柱斜撑在将倒的墙边，墙面因此重新立直
scene: 球队连败之后，教练公开肯定队员的努力，士气才慢慢回来。The new evidence bolstered the prosecution's case.
sceneCN: 这里 bolster 指为论证增加支撑、使其更有力（第 5 个义项：加强论证）；句意为新证据加强了控方的论证。

senses.title: Support something already there
senses.definition: to support or reinforce something that is already present but weak
senses.definitionCN: 支撑或加固已经存在但脆弱的东西
senses.example: Extra beams were added to bolster the old roof.
senses.exampleCN: 又加了几根梁来加固旧屋顶。
senses.why: A bolster is a cushion placed under something to hold it up, so the verb begins as a physical prop.
senses.whyCN: bolster 本是一种塞在下面托住东西的垫枕，因此动词最初是物理支撑。

senses.title: Raise confidence
senses.definition: to improve someone's confidence or sense of security
senses.definitionCN: 提高某人的信心或安全感
senses.example: The coach's praise bolstered the young players.
senses.exampleCN: 教练的赞扬增强了年轻球员的信心。
senses.why: Confidence is a structure that can sag; support under it keeps the structure standing.
senses.whyCN: 信心是一种会下垂的结构；在下面加支撑就能让它立住。

senses.title: A long cushion
senses.definition: a long, firm cushion used on a bed or sofa
senses.definitionCN: 床或沙发上使用的长而硬的垫枕
senses.example: She placed a bolster behind her back.
senses.exampleCN: 她在背后放了一个长枕。
senses.why: The noun is the object that gave the verb its image: a cushion shaped to hold a body or a wall in place.
senses.whyCN: 名词是给动词提供意象的物件：一个形状适合托住身体或墙面的垫子。

senses.title: Prop something up physically
senses.definition: to raise or hold something with a support underneath
senses.definitionCN: 用下方的支撑把某物垫高或托住
senses.example: He bolstered the crate with two blocks of wood.
senses.exampleCN: 他用两块木头垫住了木箱。
senses.why: This is the concrete ancestor of every figurative use: a thing is placed under another thing so it cannot fall.
senses.whyCN: 这是所有比喻用法具体的前身：把一物置于另一物之下，使它不会倒下。

senses.title: Strengthen an argument
senses.definition: to add evidence or force to a claim or case
senses.definitionCN: 为某项主张或论证增加证据与力度
senses.example: The new evidence bolstered the prosecution's case.
senses.exampleCN: 新证据加强了控方的论证。
senses.why: A case is a structure of reasons; each new piece of evidence is a beam under it.
senses.whyCN: 论证是由理由构成的结构；每一份新证据都是它下面的一根梁。

senses.title: Shore up a market or currency
senses.definition: to intervene to keep a market, price or currency from falling
senses.definitionCN: 通过干预防止市场、价格或货币下跌
senses.example: The central bank bolstered the currency with reserves.
senses.exampleCN: 中央银行用储备支撑本国货币。
senses.why: A falling price is a wall leaning over; intervention puts a prop under it before it collapses.
senses.whyCN: 下跌的价格是一堵倾斜的墙；干预在它倒塌之前塞进一根支柱。

senses.title: Reinforce a defense
senses.definition: to strengthen a defensive position or force
senses.definitionCN: 加强防御阵地或防御力量
senses.example: Troops were sent to bolster the northern defenses.
senses.exampleCN: 部队被派去加固北部防线。
senses.why: Defense is literally a wall, so the oldest meaning of the word returns without any metaphor at all.
senses.whyCN: 防御字面上就是一堵墙，于是这个词最古老的含义无需任何比喻就回来了。

senses.title: Act as a support against pressure
senses.definition: to serve as the thing that keeps another from giving way
senses.definitionCN: 充当使另一物不致屈服的东西
senses.example: Allies bolstered the small state against pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 盟国支撑这个小国抵御压力。
senses.why: The word can describe the prop rather than the act of propping: to be the support is also to bolster.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以描述支撑物而非支撑动作：成为支撑也就是 bolster。

intro.en: Bolster began as the name of a long cushion, and the verb grew from the cushion's job of holding things up.
intro.cn: bolster 最初是一种长枕的名称，动词由垫枕「托住东西」的功能发展而来。

items.en: The noun is old in English; the figurative verb 'to support' appears by the 16c. and is now the dominant use.
items.cn: 这个名词在英语中很古老；比喻性的动词「支持」到十六世纪出现，如今已是主要用法。

items.en: Old English bolster named a cushion or pillow, especially one stuffed with hair or straw.
items.cn: 古英语 bolster 指垫枕，尤指填有毛发或稻草的枕头。

items.en: The word belongs to a Germanic family connected with swelling and stuffing, the idea of a bag filled out to hold weight.
items.cn: 这个词属于一个日耳曼词族，与「鼓起、填塞」有关，即一个被填满以承重的袋子。

items.en: Middle English kept the noun for bed cushions and began using it for any prop placed under a heavy object.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了这个表示床枕的名词，并开始用它指垫在重物下方的任何支撑物。

items.en: From roofs and crates the verb moved to confidence, evidence, markets and defenses, wherever a structure might sag.
items.cn: 从屋顶与木箱出发，这个动词转向信心、证据、市场与防御，凡是结构可能下垂之处都可使用。

note.en: The look-alike group shares spelling or the cushion root; the near-meaning group names ways of holding something up.
note.cn: 形近组共享拼写或「垫枕」词根；近义组列出托住某物的各种方式。

entries.definition: a case for carrying a handgun, unrelated in meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 携带手枪的皮套，词义无关。

entries.definition: to fit furniture with cushions and covering.

entries.definition: to bear weight or keep something from falling.

entries.definition: to make a structure or force stronger.

entries.definition: to support with a projecting structure or with reasons.
entries.definitionCN: 用外撑结构或理由支撑。

entries.definition: to support something weak so it does not collapse.
entries.definitionCN: 支撑脆弱之物以免倒塌。

normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把「垫在歪墙下的枕头」留住。

normal.en: A bolster is a cushion put under something; the verb is that cushion's job.
normal.cn: bolster 是垫在下面的枕头；动词就是枕头的工作。

normal.en: Picture a beam leaning against a wall that is about to fall.
normal.cn: 想象一根梁斜靠在即将倒塌的墙上。

normal.en: Confidence, evidence and markets are all walls that can lean.
normal.cn: 信心、证据与市场都是可能倾斜的墙。

normal.en: Say BOL-ster, with the stress on the cushion itself.
normal.cn: 读成 BOL-ster，重音落在「垫枕」上。

normal.en: Link it with upholster: both words hide a cushion inside.
normal.cn: 把它和 upholster 联系：两个词里都藏着一个垫子。

abstract.en: Every figurative use keeps the geometry of one thing placed under another.
abstract.cn: 每个比喻用法都保留「一物置于另一物之下」的几何关系。

abstract.en: Support must arrive before collapse, which is why the word suggests urgency.
abstract.cn: 支撑必须在倒塌之前到达，所以这个词带有紧迫感。

abstract.en: To be the prop is also to bolster, so allies and evidence can share the name.
abstract.cn: 成为支撑物也就是 bolster，因此盟友与证据可以共用这个词。

examples.en: The new evidence bolstered the prosecution's case.
examples.cn: 新证据加强了控方的论证。

examples.en: The central bank moved to bolster the currency.
examples.cn: 中央银行采取行动支撑本国货币。

examples.en: Extra beams were added to bolster the old roof.
examples.cn: 又加了几根梁来加固旧屋顶。

dict_mnemonic.text: bolster 本是「长枕」：把枕头垫在要倒的东西下面，就是「支撑、加强」。

root: 古英语 bolster（垫枕），属日耳曼语族，与「填塞、鼓起」有关

sensesIntro.en: Bolster always places support under something; the senses differ in whether the thing supported is a roof, a currency, a case, a defense or a person's confidence.
sensesIntro.cn: bolster 始终是在某物下方加支撑；各义项的差别在于被支撑的是屋顶、货币、论证、防御还是人的信心。

core.en: A PROP UNDER A SAGGING STRUCTURE
core.cn: 倾斜结构下的一根支柱

branches.en: The literal act of holding something up.
branches.cn: 把某物托住的字面动作。

branches.en: Confidence and allies that keep a person or state from giving way.
branches.cn: 使个人或国家不致屈服的信心与盟友。

branches.en: The cushion that gave the word its shape.

branches.en: Evidence placed under a legal case.

definition_zh: 官僚；官吏；拘泥程序的官员；公务员
definition_en: an official working in a large administrative system, often seen as rule-bound
core_image: 窗口后面的人把表格推回来，手指点在第三个空格上，要求重填
scene: 办证窗口后面的人把表格推回来，指着第三个空格要求重填。The clerk was a career bureaucrat who knew every form by number.
sceneCN: 这里 bureaucrat 指长期在行政系统内按规章办事的官员（第 2 个义项：拘泥程序的官员）；句意为这名职员是职业官僚，能凭编号记住每一种表格。

senses.title: An official in a bureaucracy
senses.definition: a person employed in a large administrative system, working within its rules
senses.definitionCN: 受雇于庞大行政系统、在其规则内工作的人
senses.example: Every form passes through three bureaucrats before approval.
senses.exampleCN: 每份表格在批准前要经过三位官员。
senses.why: Bureau meant a desk, and the suffix named rule by desks: the person is defined by the office rather than by a craft.
senses.whyCN: bureau 原指书桌，词尾表示「由书桌统治」：这个人由职位而非手艺来定义。

senses.title: A rule-bound official
senses.definition: an official who follows procedure rigidly, even when the rule defeats its purpose
senses.definitionCN: 严格遵循程序、即使规则违背目的也不变通的官员
senses.example: The clerk was a career bureaucrat who knew every form by number.
senses.exampleCN: 这名职员是职业官僚，能凭编号记住每一种表格。
senses.why: Procedure protects against favouritism, but the same protection can become a wall between the official and the person in front of the window.
senses.whyCN: 程序可以防止徇私，但同样的保护也可能变成官员与窗口前那个人之间的一堵墙。

senses.title: A term of criticism
senses.definition: a label for someone seen as caring more about process than about people
senses.definitionCN: 指被看作只重流程、不重人的那种人
senses.example: The minister dismissed the objections as the work of bureaucrats.
senses.exampleCN: 部长把反对意见斥为官僚之作。
senses.why: When the word is used as an insult, it says the person has become the rule he or she applies.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词被当作侮辱使用时，它是在说这个人已经变成了自己所执行的规则。

senses.title: A senior civil servant
senses.definition: a career administrator with substantial authority inside government
senses.definitionCN: 在政府内部拥有实质权力的职业行政官
senses.example: A senior bureaucrat drafted the new regulation.
senses.exampleCN: 一位高级文官起草了新规。
senses.why: At the top of the system the same word can be neutral or respectful: experience in procedure becomes expertise.
senses.whyCN: 在系统顶端，同一个词可以是中性甚至尊重的：程序经验变成了专业能力。

senses.title: A management type
senses.definition: in organization theory, a role defined by office rules rather than by personal ownership
senses.definitionCN: 在组织理论中，由职位规则而非个人所有权界定的角色
senses.example: Weber described the bureaucrat as a salaried office holder.
senses.exampleCN: 韦伯把官僚描述为领取薪水的职位持有者。
senses.why: Organization theory looks at the role rather than the person: a salaried holder of defined duties is a structure, not a character.
senses.whyCN: 组织理论看的是角色而不是人：领取薪水、职责明确的持有者是一种结构，而不是一个性格。

senses.title: A minor functionary
senses.definition: a low-ranking official with narrow, tightly defined authority
senses.definitionCN: 职权狭窄、界定严格的下级官员
senses.example: A petty bureaucrat can stop a project with one stamp.
senses.exampleCN: 一个小官僚用一个印章就能让项目停摆。
senses.why: Small authority feels large because it sits at a narrow gate; the word measures the gate, not the person.
senses.whyCN: 微小的权力之所以显得巨大，是因为它守着一道窄门；这个词衡量的是门，而不是人。

senses.title: An official of a party or movement
senses.definition: an official whose position comes from a party or movement organization
senses.definitionCN: 职位来自政党或运动组织的官员
senses.example: Party bureaucrats controlled the local allocation of housing.
senses.exampleCN: 党务官僚控制着当地的住房分配。
senses.why: A party adds loyalty to procedure, so the same office gains a second source of authority and a second reason to resist change.
senses.whyCN: 政党为程序加上忠诚，于是同一职位获得了第二个权威来源，也获得了第二个抗拒改变的理由。

senses.title: An administrator in a large firm
senses.definition: an administrator in a large company, often criticized for slow process
senses.definitionCN: 大公司里的行政人员，常因流程缓慢而受批评
senses.example: The engineers blamed corporate bureaucrats for the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师把延误归咎于企业官僚。
senses.why: The desk and the rule move into private companies unchanged, which is why the word follows administration wherever it grows.
senses.whyCN: 书桌与规则原封不动地进入私营公司，因此这个词会跟随行政机构的扩张而出现。

intro.en: Bureaucrat is a French coinage from bureau, a desk, and -crate, rule: rule by desks.
intro.cn: bureaucrat 是法语新造词，由 bureau（书桌）与 -crate（统治）构成，意为「书桌的统治」。

items.en: English adopted bureaucrat in the 19c. along with bureaucracy, as large state administrations took shape.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪随着大型国家行政机构成形，与 bureaucracy 一同吸收 bureaucrat。

items.en: French bureaucrate was formed in the early 19c. from bureau and the Greek suffix -krates 'ruler'.
items.cn: 法语 bureaucrate 在十九世纪初由 bureau 与希腊词尾 -krates「统治者」构成。

items.en: Bureau first meant a coarse cloth covering a desk, then the desk itself, then the office and the organization.
items.cn: bureau 最初指盖在书桌上的粗布，后来指书桌本身，再指办公室与机构。

items.en: The suffix -krates comes from kratos 'power, rule', also seen in democrat and aristocrat.
items.cn: 词尾 -krates 来自 kratos「权力、统治」，也见于 democrat 与 aristocrat。

items.en: As administrations grew, the word acquired its sneer: the official who serves the rule instead of the public.
items.cn: 随着行政机构扩张，这个词带上了讥讽：服务规则而非公众的官员。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the bureau stem; the near-meaning group names people inside administrative systems.
note.cn: 形近组共享 bureau 词干；近义组列出行政系统中的人物。

normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把单词拆成「书桌」与「统治者」。

normal.cn: bureau 意为书桌，crat 意为统治者：bureaucrat 就是坐在书桌后的统治者。

normal.en: Picture a window, a stamp and a form with one box still empty.
normal.cn: 想象一个窗口、一枚印章，以及一张还空着一格的表格。

normal.en: The -crat ending appears in democrat and aristocrat, all naming who rules.
normal.cn: 词尾 -crat 也见于 democrat 与 aristocrat，都命名谁在统治。

normal.en: Say byoo-ROH-krat, with the desk in the first half.
normal.cn: 读成 byoo-ROH-krat，前半段就是书桌。

normal.en: Link it with bureaucracy: the person and the system share the same desk.
normal.cn: 把它和 bureaucracy 联系：人与制度共享同一张书桌。

abstract.en: Small authority at a narrow gate feels large to whoever stands outside.
abstract.cn: 窄门上的微小权力，对门外的人而言显得巨大。

abstract.en: At the top of the system the same word turns into expertise.

examples.en: The clerk was a career bureaucrat who knew every form by number.

definition_zh: 强制的；胁迫的；用武力迫使的
definition_en: using pressure, threats or force to make someone act against their own preference
core_image: 一扇门被从外面顶住，里面的人只能往唯一的方向退
scene: 会议室里没有人投反对票，因为先前反对的人已经被请出去了。The agreement was coercive rather than freely negotiated.
sceneCN: 这里 coercive 指以强制手段迫使对方接受（第 1 个义项：以强制迫使人行动）；句意为这份协议是强制达成的，而不是自由谈成的。

senses.title: Forcing someone to act
senses.definition: using pressure, threats or force to make a person act against their preference
senses.definitionCN: 以压力、威胁或武力使某人违背自己意愿行事
senses.example: The agreement was coercive rather than freely negotiated.
senses.exampleCN: 这份协议是强制达成的，而不是自由谈成的。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to shut in together': the pressured person is given no room to move except the one chosen by the other side.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「一起关起来」：被施压者除了对方选定的方向之外，没有可移动的余地。

senses.title: Backed by penalties
senses.definition: of a rule or measure, enforced by penalties rather than by persuasion
senses.definitionCN: 指规则或措施靠惩罚而非说服来执行
senses.example: The city imposed coercive fines on illegal dumping.
senses.exampleCN: 该市对非法倾倒处以强制罚款。
senses.why: A rule without a penalty is advice; the penalty is what closes the exit and makes the rule coercive.
senses.whyCN: 没有惩罚的规则只是建议；惩罚封住出口，才使规则具有强制性。

senses.title: Power that punishes
senses.definition: in politics, power resting on the ability to punish or deprive
senses.definitionCN: 在政治学中，指建立在惩罚或剥夺能力之上的权力
senses.example: The regime relied on coercive power rather than legitimacy.
senses.exampleCN: 该政权依靠强制力而非合法性。
senses.why: Power can persuade, reward or punish; the coercive kind works by making refusal expensive.
senses.whyCN: 权力可以说服、给予或惩罚；强制性的那一种通过让拒绝变得昂贵来起作用。

senses.title: A pressuring tone
senses.definition: of speech, pressing the listener rather than inviting a response
senses.definitionCN: 指言语压迫听者，而不是邀请回应
senses.example: His coercive tone ended the discussion before it began.
senses.exampleCN: 他带有压迫感的语气让讨论还没开始就结束了。
senses.why: Tone can close a conversation the way a fine closes a road; the listener is still present but has no way through.
senses.whyCN: 语气可以像罚款封路那样封住对话；听者仍在场，却无路可走。

senses.title: Bargaining under threat
senses.definition: of negotiation, conducted while one side holds a threat over the other
senses.definitionCN: 指谈判在一方对另一方持有威胁的情况下进行
senses.example: The strike turned the talks into coercive bargaining.
senses.exampleCN: 罢工把谈判变成了胁迫性谈判。
senses.why: A bargain assumes both sides may walk away; a threat removes that option, so the agreement is signed under pressure.
senses.whyCN: 交易假定双方都可以走开；威胁移除了这个选项，于是协议在压力下签署。

senses.title: Involuntary treatment
senses.definition: in psychiatry or law, treatment given without the patient's consent
senses.definitionCN: 在精神医学或法律中，未经病人同意而给予的治疗
senses.example: The court authorized coercive treatment for the patient.
senses.exampleCN: 法院批准对该病人实施强制治疗。
senses.why: When a person cannot consent safely, the law may replace consent with authority, and the word marks that substitution.
senses.whyCN: 当一个人无法安全地作出同意时，法律可能用权威取代同意，而这个词标记的正是这种取代。

senses.title: Forced recruitment
senses.definition: of recruitment, compelling people into service against their will
senses.definitionCN: 指违背本人意愿迫使人们服役
senses.example: Coercive recruitment filled the ranks with unwilling soldiers.
senses.exampleCN: 强制征募用不情愿的士兵填满了队伍。
senses.why: A volunteer army relies on choice; conscription replaces choice with a penalty for refusal, which is the definition of coercion.
senses.whyCN: 志愿军依靠选择；征兵用「拒绝即受罚」取代选择，这正是强制的定义。

senses.title: An environment with no real exit
senses.definition: of a setting or relationship, where refusing carries a cost that makes consent nominal
senses.definitionCN: 指环境或关系中，拒绝要付出代价，使「同意」只是名义上的
senses.example: The workers described a coercive environment with no real exit.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们描述了一个没有真实退路的强制环境。
senses.why: The last sense is structural: nothing is said aloud, but every option except one has been quietly priced out.
senses.whyCN: 最后一个义项是结构性的：没有任何明说，但除了一种选择之外，其余选择都被悄然标上了高昂代价。

intro.en: Coercive comes from a Latin verb meaning to shut in or restrain, built from 'together' and 'enclose'.
intro.cn: coercive 来自一个意为「关起来、约束」的拉丁动词，由「一起」与「围住」构成。

items.en: English formed coercive in the 17c. from coercion, and modern politics uses it for power that punishes.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪由 coercion 造出 coercive；现代政治学用它指以惩罚为基础的权力。

items.en: Coercere meant 'to shut in, restrain, compel', formed from co- 'together' and arcere 'to enclose, keep off'.
items.cn: coercere 意为「关住、约束、强迫」，由 co-「一起」与 arcere「围住、挡住」构成。

items.en: Arcere 'to enclose, ward off' also underlies the noun arx, a citadel, and the English word arcane through a different path.
items.cn: arcere「围住、挡开」也构成名词 arx（城堡），并通过另一条路径与英语 arcane 相关。

items.en: Roman law used coercitio for the magistrate's power to compel obedience by fines and arrest.
items.cn: 罗马法用 coercitio 指长官通过罚款与拘捕强制服从的权力。

items.en: The word widened from courts to workplaces and families, where pressure can compel without any visible force.
items.cn: 这个词从法庭扩展到职场与家庭，在这些地方，压力无需可见的武力也能迫使行动。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the coercion stem; the near-meaning group names kinds of compulsion.
note.cn: 形近组共享 coercion 词干；近义组列出各种强迫。

definition_zh: 有助于……的；促成……的；有利的
definition_en: tending to help bring about a result or to make a condition favourable
core_image: 一扇窗被推开一条缝，风顺着进来，桌上的火苗因此烧得更稳
scene: 图书馆把灯调到柔和，桌上只留一盏小台灯，翻书声几乎听不见。A quiet room is conducive to concentrated work.
sceneCN: 这里 conducive 指某种条件有助于产生专注工作这一结果（第 1 个义项：有助于某结果）；句意为安静的房间有助于集中精力工作。

pos.zh: 有助于……的；促成……的；有利的

senses.title: Helping bring about a result
senses.definition: tending to make a particular result more likely or easier
senses.definitionCN: 使某个特定结果更可能出现或更容易实现
senses.example: A quiet room is conducive to concentrated work.
senses.exampleCN: 安静的房间有助于集中精力工作。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to lead together': conditions walk beside a result and help it arrive.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「共同引导」：条件伴随结果同行，帮助它抵达。

senses.title: A favourable setting
senses.definition: of a place or atmosphere, favourable to a stated activity
senses.definitionCN: 指场所或氛围对某项活动有利
senses.example: The new studio is conducive to collaboration.
senses.exampleCN: 新的工作室有利于协作。
senses.why: A setting is not the work itself, but it can remove friction, and removing friction is what 'conducive' praises.
senses.whyCN: 环境本身不是工作，但它可以消除摩擦，而消除摩擦正是 conducive 所称赞的。

senses.title: Good for health
senses.definition: of conditions, helping the body stay well
senses.definitionCN: 指条件有助于身体保持健康
senses.example: Dry air and long walks are conducive to health.
senses.exampleCN: 干燥的空气与长距离散步有益健康。
senses.why: The body responds to conditions before it responds to intentions, so the weather and the walking path are part of the treatment.
senses.whyCN: 身体先对条件作出反应，再对意图作出反应，因此天气与步行的路径也是治疗的一部分。

senses.title: Supporting learning
senses.definition: of arrangements, making learning easier or more effective
senses.definitionCN: 指安排使学习更容易或更有效
senses.example: Small classes are conducive to discussion.
senses.exampleCN: 小班教学有利于讨论。
senses.why: Learning needs room for a voice to be heard and answered, and a small class supplies that room.
senses.whyCN: 学习需要有让声音被听见并获得回应的空间，小班正好提供这个空间。

senses.title: Likely to cause error
senses.definition: of conditions, making mistakes more likely
senses.definitionCN: 指条件使错误更可能发生
senses.example: Too little sleep is conducive to error.
senses.exampleCN: 睡眠不足容易导致出错。
senses.why: The word is neutral about the outcome: the same machinery that helps a good result can help a bad one.
senses.whyCN: 这个词对结果本身是中性的：帮助好结果的同一套机制，也能帮助坏结果。

senses.title: Helping peace
senses.definition: of measures or attitudes, making peace more likely
senses.definitionCN: 指措施或态度使和平更可能
senses.example: Open trade routes were conducive to peace.
senses.exampleCN: 开放的贸易路线有助于和平。
senses.why: Contact between groups gives each side something to lose, and that shared stake makes war less attractive.
senses.whyCN: 群体间的往来让每一方都有可失去之物，这份共同利害使战争不那么有吸引力。

senses.title: Suited to a purpose
senses.definition: of an arrangement, well suited to the end it is meant to serve
senses.definitionCN: 指安排很适合它所要服务的目的
senses.example: The seating plan was conducive to a short ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 这样的座位安排适合一场简短的仪式。
senses.why: Every plan has a clock and a shape; arrangement is the part that lets the clock run without obstruction.
senses.whyCN: 每个计划都有自己的时钟与形状；安排就是让时钟不受阻碍地运行的那一部分。

senses.title: Allowing a process to run
senses.definition: of scientific or technical conditions, permitting a process to occur
senses.definitionCN: 指科学或技术条件允许某个过程发生
senses.example: Constant temperature is conducive to crystal growth.
senses.exampleCN: 恒温有利于晶体生长。
senses.why: A process needs its conditions held steady; when the surroundings stop interfering, the process can proceed on its own.
senses.whyCN: 过程需要条件保持稳定；当周围停止干扰，过程便能自行推进。

intro.en: Conducive comes from a Latin verb meaning to lead together, the same root as conduct.
intro.cn: conducive 来自一个意为「共同引导」的拉丁动词，与 conduct 同根。

items.en: English formed conducive in the 19c. from the verb conduce, originally in the sense of contributing to a result.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪由动词 conduce 造出 conducive，原义是「对结果有贡献」。

items.en: Conducere meant 'to lead together, bring along, contribute', from com- 'together' and ducere 'to lead'.
items.cn: conducere 意为「共同引导、带来、促成」，由 com-「一起」与 ducere「引导」构成。

items.en: Ducere 'to lead' gives conduct, duct, deduce and educate, all built on the image of a path being led.
items.cn: ducere「引导」产生 conduct、duct、deduce 与 educate，都建立在「引路」的意象上。

items.en: The fixed pattern 'conducive to' became standard in the 20c., especially in medicine, education and social science.
items.cn: 固定搭配 conducive to 在二十世纪成为标准用法，尤其在医学、教育与社会科学的文本中。

items.en: The word now covers settings, habits and policies, anywhere conditions can help an outcome along.
items.cn: 这个词如今覆盖环境、习惯与政策，凡条件能推动结果之处都可使用。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the leading root or looks similar; the near-meaning group names ways of helping a result.
note.cn: 形近组共享「引导」词根或拼写相近；近义组列出帮助结果发生的各种方式。

abstract.en: A setting is not the work, but it can take the friction out of the work.

abstract.en: Conditions lead results the way a channel leads water.

examples.en: Too little sleep is conducive to error.

definition_zh: 大批毁灭；严重削弱；杀死十分之一（古义）
definition_en: to destroy a large proportion of something, or in the old Roman sense to kill one in every ten
core_image: 一排士兵抽签，每十个人里有一人向前一步，走向另一侧
scene: 一场疫病过后，村里的羊只剩不到三成。The epidemic decimated the herd within a single season.
sceneCN: 这里 decimate 指疫病大批杀死牲畜、使群体所剩无几（第 1 个义项：大批毁灭）；句意为这场疫病在一个季节内就让羊群大批死亡。

pos.zh: 大批毁灭；严重削弱；杀死十分之一（古义）

derivatives.zh: 大批毁灭；古代十一抽杀

senses.title: Destroy a large proportion
senses.definition: to kill or destroy a large part of a group or population
senses.definitionCN: 杀死或毁掉一个群体或人口中的大部分
senses.example: The epidemic decimated the herd within a single season.
senses.exampleCN: 这场疫病在一个季节内就让羊群大批死亡。
senses.why: The Roman punishment took one in ten; over time the word's force grew until it meant a heavy loss rather than an exact tenth.
senses.whyCN: 罗马的惩罚是十人杀一；随着时间推移，这个词的力度增大，指惨重损失，而不再指精确的十分之一。

senses.title: Severely weaken
senses.definition: to reduce the strength or effectiveness of something drastically
senses.definitionCN: 大幅降低某物的力量或效力
senses.example: The scandal decimated the party's credibility.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻严重削弱了该党的公信力。
senses.why: A group can be hit without being killed: when every tenth member is removed, the remaining body cannot work as before.
senses.whyCN: 群体可以被打击而不被杀死：每十人中失去一人，剩下的身体也无法像从前那样运作。

senses.title: The Roman punishment
senses.definition: in Roman history, to kill one soldier in every ten as a unit punishment
senses.definitionCN: 在罗马史中，作为部队惩罚，每十名士兵处死一名
senses.example: The legion was decimated after the mutiny.
senses.exampleCN: 哗变之后，这个军团被施以十一抽杀。
senses.why: The original sense is exact: decem is ten, and the punishment was counted out one by one.
senses.whyCN: 原义是精确的：decem 就是十，惩罚是一个一个数出来的。

senses.title: Devastate by disease or war
senses.titleCN: 疫病或战争造成大量死亡
senses.definition: of disease, war or disaster, to kill many members of a population
senses.definitionCN: 指疾病、战争或灾难使人口大量死亡
senses.example: Smallpox decimated the villages along the river.
senses.exampleCN: 天花使沿河的村庄人口大减。
senses.why: When the cause is invisible, the arithmetic is still visible in the empty houses left behind.
senses.whyCN: 当原因看不见时，算术仍留在空置的房屋里。

senses.title: Take a tenth, in old use
senses.definition: in older use, to take a tenth of something, especially as a tax
senses.definitionCN: 在较早用法中，取走某物的十分之一，尤指作为税
senses.example: The old chronicle says the ruler decimated the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 旧编年史说统治者抽取了收成的十分之一。
senses.why: The word carries both a fraction and a blow: a tenth can be a lawful share or a lethal cut, depending on who counts.
senses.whyCN: 这个词同时带着分数与打击：十分之一可以是合法份额，也可以是致命削减，取决于谁来数。

senses.title: Thin out a group
senses.definition: to remove a large number of members from a group, often at random
senses.definitionCN: 从群体中大量移除成员，常带有随机性
senses.example: The layoffs decimated the research division.
senses.exampleCN: 裁员让研究部门的人数锐减。
senses.why: Removal at random feels like a lottery, which is close to the original punishment's method of choosing.
senses.whyCN: 随机移除感觉像抽签，这与原初惩罚的挑选方式相近。

senses.title: Ruin a place
senses.definition: of a place, to damage it so severely that little remains intact
senses.definitionCN: 指把某地破坏到几乎不剩完整之物
senses.example: Repeated fires decimated the old town.
senses.exampleCN: 反复的火灾毁掉了这座老城。
senses.why: A place is a collection of structures and people; remove enough of either and the whole stops functioning as a town.
senses.whyCN: 一个地方是建筑与人的集合；移除其中任何一方足够多，整体就不再作为城镇运作。

senses.title: Shrink a population in ecology
senses.definition: in ecology, to reduce a population sharply, often below a viable level
senses.definitionCN: 在生态学中，使种群骤减，常低于可维持水平
senses.example: Invasive species decimated the native frogs.
senses.exampleCN: 入侵物种使本地蛙类数量骤减。
senses.why: A population needs a minimum number to breed and recover; below that line, a heavy loss becomes a permanent one.
senses.whyCN: 种群需要最低数量才能繁殖与恢复；低于这条线，惨重损失就变成永久损失。

intro.en: Decimate comes from the Latin word for ten and originally named a Roman punishment of one in ten.
intro.cn: decimate 来自拉丁语中表示「十」的词，最初命名罗马「十人杀一」的惩罚。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the 17c. for the Roman punishment, and by the 19c. it was used for any heavy loss.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个动词，指罗马的惩罚；到十九世纪，它已用于任何惨重损失。

items.en: Decimare meant 'to take a tenth' and, in the army, 'to punish by killing one in ten'.
items.cn: decimare 意为「取十分之一」，在军队中意为「以十人杀一的方式惩罚」。

items.en: Decem is the Latin word for ten, the source of decimal and December, the tenth month of the old calendar.
items.cn: decem 是拉丁语「十」，是 decimal 与 December（旧历的第十个月）的来源。

items.en: A unit that had disgraced itself was divided into groups of ten and each group drew lots for one to be beaten or killed.
items.cn: 蒙羞的部队被分成十人一组，每组抽签选出一人受鞭打或处死。

items.en: Usage guides long argued that the word should mean exactly one in ten, but the wider sense of heavy loss now dominates.
items.cn: 用法指南长期主张这个词应精确表示「十分之一」，但如今「惨重损失」的宽泛义已占主导。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ten root; the near-meaning group names kinds of large destruction.
note.cn: 形近组共享「十」词根；近义组列出大规模毁灭的各种方式。

definition_zh: 礼仪；得体；端庄；合乎场合的举止
definition_en: correct and dignified behaviour that suits the occasion and shows self-control
core_image: 葬礼上所有人压低声音，手机收进口袋，动作放慢半拍
scene: 葬礼上没有人高声说话，连手机都收进了口袋。The guests observed decorum even when the speech went wrong.
sceneCN: 这里 decorum 指合乎场合、保持端庄的举止（第 1 个义项：得体举止）；句意为即使致辞出了差错，宾客们仍遵守礼仪。

pos.zh: 礼仪；得体；端庄；合乎场合的举止

senses.title: Proper behaviour in public
senses.definition: conformity to accepted standards of polite behaviour in public
senses.definitionCN: 符合公共场合公认的礼貌行为标准
senses.example: The guests observed decorum even when the speech went wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 即使致辞出了差错，宾客们仍遵守礼仪。
senses.why: The Latin word named 'that which is fitting'; decorum is the behaviour that fits a room the way a key fits a lock.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词命名「合适之物」；decorum 就是像钥匙配锁那样契合场合的行为。

senses.title: A dignified appearance
senses.definition: an impression of seriousness, self-control and good form
senses.definitionCN: 严肃、自持与良好仪态给人的印象
senses.example: He received the award with quiet decorum.
senses.exampleCN: 他以安静的端庄接受了奖项。
senses.why: Appearance is the visible edge of behaviour: a straightened back and a low voice announce that the occasion is being respected.
senses.whyCN: 仪表是行为可见的边缘：挺直的背与压低的声音宣告对场合的尊重。

senses.title: Rules of a formal occasion
senses.definition: the set of customs expected at a ceremony or formal event
senses.definitionCN: 典礼或正式活动中被期待的一套习俗
senses.example: The ushers were briefed on the decorum of the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 引座员被告知典礼的礼仪要求。
senses.why: When many people share one event, expected behaviour becomes a script, and decorum is the script being followed.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人共享一个场合，被期待的行为就变成脚本，而 decorum 就是被遵循的脚本。

senses.title: Suitability of style
senses.definition: in literary criticism, the fitting of style to subject and occasion
senses.definitionCN: 在文学批评中，指风格与题材、场合的相称
senses.example: Classical critics made decorum a rule of style.
senses.exampleCN: 古典批评家把得体定为风格规则。
senses.why: A style is also behaviour: a grand subject refuses a joke, and the critic calls the refusal decorum.
senses.whyCN: 风格也是一种行为：宏大的题材拒绝玩笑，而批评家把这种拒绝称为得体。

senses.title: Composure under pressure
senses.definition: calm and correct behaviour maintained when something goes wrong
senses.definitionCN: 出差错时仍保持的镇定与正确举止
senses.example: She kept her decorum while the accusation was read aloud.
senses.exampleCN: 指控被朗读时，她仍保持镇定得体。
senses.why: The test of a standard is the moment it becomes inconvenient; decorum is most visible when it costs something.
senses.whyCN: 标准在它变得不方便的那一刻才受到检验；得体在需要付出代价时最为显眼。

senses.title: Ceremonial order
senses.definition: the prescribed order and manner of a formal ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 正式仪式规定的次序与方式
senses.example: The procession followed the decorum of the old rite.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍遵循古老仪式的既定次序。
senses.why: A ceremony is a sequence that must not be rearranged, and decorum is that sequence made visible in bodies.
senses.whyCN: 典礼是一套不可重排的次序，而得体就是这套次序在身体上的显现。

senses.title: Expected tone in scholarship
senses.titleCN: 学术写作中的得体语气
senses.definition: the tone and restraint expected in academic or professional writing
senses.definitionCN: 学术或专业写作中被期待的语调与克制
senses.example: The journal asked for decorum in the response.
senses.exampleCN: 期刊要求回应保持学术得体。
senses.why: Written exchange has its own room to fit: certain claims can be made, but not in certain voices.
senses.whyCN: 书面往来也有自己要契合的房间：某些主张可以提出，但不能以某些声音提出。

senses.title: Outward correctness as a mask
senses.definition: correct outward form that may conceal disorder underneath
senses.definitionCN: 外表的正确可能掩盖内在的失序
senses.example: The family maintained decorum while the argument continued upstairs.
senses.exampleCN: 楼上的争吵还在继续，一家人却维持着表面的得体。
senses.why: Form can be kept after feeling has gone, so the word can name a surface that no longer reports what is beneath it.
senses.whyCN: 感受消失后形式仍可维持，因此这个词也能命名一个不再反映内里的表面。

intro.en: Decorum is Latin for 'that which is fitting', from a root meaning grace and dignity.
intro.cn: decorum 是拉丁语「合适之物」的意思，词根意为优雅与尊严。

items.en: English borrowed decorum in the 17c. as a term of social and literary criticism.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 decorum，作为社会与文学批评的术语。

items.en: Decorum was the neuter of decorus 'fitting, graceful', used as a noun for what is proper.
items.cn: decorum 是 decorus「合适、优雅」的中性形式，作名词指合宜之物。

items.en: Decus meant 'grace, dignity, ornament', and gives decorate and decoration through related forms.
items.cn: decus 意为「优雅、尊严、装饰」，通过相关形式产生 decorate 与 decoration。

items.en: The impersonal verb decet 'it is fitting' states the standard that decorum later names.
items.cn: 无人称动词 decet「这是合适的」陈述了 decorum 后来命名的标准。

items.en: From public manners the word moved to literary style and then to any setting where a correct form is expected.
items.cn: 这个词从公共礼仪转向文学风格，再转向任何期待正确形式的场合。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the fitting root; the near-meaning group names codes of proper behaviour.
note.cn: 形近组共享「合适」词根；近义组列出得体行为的各种规范。

normal.cn: 想想 decor 与 decoration：适合房间、让一切显得恰当的东西。

normal.en: Picture a funeral where voices drop and phones disappear.
normal.cn: 想象一场葬礼，声音压低，手机消失。

normal.en: Decorum is behaviour that fits the occasion the way a key fits its lock.
normal.cn: decorum 是契合场合的行为，就像钥匙契合锁。

normal.en: Say de-COR-um, with the stress on the fit.
normal.cn: 读成 de-COR-um，重音落在「契合」上。

normal.en: Link it with decorous: the adjective describes the person, the noun describes the standard.
normal.cn: 把它和 decorous 联系：形容词描述人，名词描述标准。

abstract.en: A standard is tested when following it costs something.
abstract.cn: 标准在遵守它需要付出代价时受到考验。

abstract.en: Form can outlive feeling, which is why decorum can also be a mask.
abstract.cn: 形式可以比感受活得更久，所以得体也可能是一张面具。

abstract.en: Every occasion has a shape, and decorum is the body agreeing to that shape.
abstract.cn: 每个场合都有形状，decorum 就是身体对这个形状的应允。

examples.en: The guests observed decorum even when the speech went wrong.
examples.cn: 即使致辞出了差错，宾客们仍遵守礼仪。

examples.en: She kept her decorum while the accusation was read aloud.
examples.cn: 指控被朗读时，她仍保持镇定得体。

examples.en: The journal asked for decorum in the response.
examples.cn: 期刊要求回应保持学术得体。

dict_mnemonic.text: decus（优雅、合宜）+ orum：符合场合的优雅，就是「得体、礼仪」。

root: 拉丁语 decorum（合宜之物），源自 decus（优雅、尊严）

sensesIntro.en: Decorum always means fitting a form; the senses differ in whether the form belongs to a room, a face, a ceremony, a style or a profession.
sensesIntro.cn: decorum 始终表示契合某种形式；各义项的差别在于这形式属于房间、面孔、典礼、文体还是职业。

branches.en: Public manners and the rules of a formal event.
branches.cn: 公共礼仪与正式活动的规则。

branches.en: Dignified appearance and composure under pressure.
branches.cn: 端庄仪表与压力下的镇定。

branches.en: Style that suits its subject, and tone in scholarship.
branches.cn: 与题材相称的风格，以及学术语调。

branches.en: The prescribed order of a ceremony.
branches.cn: 典礼规定的次序。

branches.en: Correct form kept after the feeling has gone.
branches.cn: 感受消失后仍维持的正确形式。

intro.en: The word is a Latin neuter adjective used as a noun, and its family is the family of fitting and grace.
intro.cn: 这个词是作名词用的拉丁中性形容词，其同族词属于「合宜」与「优雅」家族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show fitness becoming a social and literary standard.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁语条目展示「合宜」如何变成社会与文学标准。

items.meaning: to add what makes a thing fitting

items.example: Decet states the standard behind decorum.
items.exampleCN: decet 陈述了 decorum 背后的标准。

items.example: Museum names a place of the Muses.
